value.zh: 身長八尺二寸，姿望秀偉，飲酒石餘，而遲鈍質樸，不為鄉親所重。
value.en: He stood eight chi and two cun tall, carried himself with striking presence, and could put away more than a shi of wine, yet he seemed slow and unpolished, so neighbors and relatives thought little of him.
value.literal: His body was eight chi two cun in height, his bearing fine and grand, he drank more than a shi of wine, yet was slow, dull, plain, and was not esteemed by townsmen and kin.

value.zh: 從叔父吏部郎衡，有名當世，亦不之知，使守水碓，每歎曰：「舒堪數百戶長，我願畢矣！」
value.en: His paternal uncle Heng, a Personnel Ministry officer celebrated in their day, never recognized his gifts either and set him to mind the water-powered mill, sighing, "If Shu can serve as headman over a few hundred households, I shall ask nothing more!"
value.literal: His father's cousin Heng, Personnel Ministry gentleman, had fame in the age, also did not know him, made him guard the water trip-hammer, and often sighed, saying, "Shu can suffice as chief of several hundred households — my wishes are fulfilled!"

value.zh: 舒亦不以介意。
value.en: Shu did not resent him for it.
value.literal: Shu also did not on that account take it to mind.

value.zh: 不修常人之節，不為皎曆之事，每欲容才長物，終不顯人之短。
value.en: He scorned petty convention and avoided ostentatious moralism, preferring always to nurture others' strengths and never to expose their faults.
value.literal: He did not cultivate ordinary men's scruples, did not do bright-harsh matters, always wished to accommodate talent and lengthen things, and to the end did not display people's shortcomings.

value.zh: 性好騎射，著韋衣。
value.en: He loved riding and archery and habitually dressed in leather hunting clothes.
value.literal: By nature he loved riding and shooting, and wore leather garments.

value.zh: 入山澤，以漁獵為事。
value.en: He roamed hills and wetlands and made fishing and hunting his chief pastime.
value.literal: He entered mountains and marshes and took fishing and hunting as his occupation.

value.zh: 唯太原王乂謂舒曰：「卿終當為台輔，然今未能令妻子免饑寒，吾當助卿營之。」
value.en: Wang Yi of Taiyuan alone told him, "You are destined for the highest councils of state, yet you cannot yet keep your wife and children from want; let me help you set them up."
value.literal: Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan said to Shu, "You in the end will become a pillar minister, yet now are not able to cause wife and children to escape cold and hunger; I shall help you arrange it."

value.zh: 常振其匱乏，舒受而不辭。
value.en: Wang regularly supplied what the household lacked, and Shu accepted without demur.
value.literal: He regularly relieved their want; Shu accepted and did not decline.

value.zh: 舒嘗詣野王，主人妻夜產，俄而聞車馬之聲，相問曰：「男也，女也？」
value.en: On a visit to Yewang, while his host's wife labored in the night, voices like chariots and horses suddenly sounded outside, asking, "Boy or girl?"
value.literal: Shu once went to Yewang; the host's wife gave birth in the night; presently they heard the sound of horses and chariots, mutually asking, "Male or female?"

value.zh: 曰：「男，書之，十五以兵死。」
value.en: The answer came: "A son. Record it—he will die by the sword at fifteen."
value.literal: It was said, "Male; write it; at fifteen he will die by weapons."

value.zh: 復問：「寢者為誰？」
value.en: Then they asked, "Who lies abed here?"
value.literal: Again they asked, "Who is the one sleeping?"

value.zh: 曰：「魏公舒。」
value.en: The reply was, "Lord Wei Shu."
value.literal: It was said, "Lord Wei Shu."

value.zh: 後十五載，詣主人，問所生兒何在，曰：「因條桑為斧傷而死。」
value.en: Fifteen years later he looked up the host and asked after that child; the man said, "He died when an axe slipped as he was pruning mulberry."
value.literal: After fifteen years he went to the host, asked where the born child was, and it was said, "Because trimming mulberry he was wounded by an axe and died."

value.zh: 舒自知當為公矣。
value.en: Shu understood then that he was fated to rise to the rank of duke.
value.literal: Shu himself knew he would become a duke.

value.zh: 高光，字宣茂，陳留圉城人，魏太尉柔之子也。
value.en: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuanmao, was a native of Yucheng in Chenliu, the son of Grand Commandant Gao Rou of Wei.
value.literal: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuanmao, was a man of Yucheng in Chenliu, son of Wei Grand Commandant Rou.

value.zh: 光少習家業，明練刑理。
value.en: From youth he trained in his family's legal tradition and became expert in penal law.
value.literal: Guang in youth practiced the family occupation, was clear and practiced in punishments and principles.

value.zh: 初以太子舍人累遷尚書郎，出為幽州刺史、潁州太守。
value.en: He began as household gentleman to the heir apparent and rose to gentleman of the masters of writing, then became inspector of You province and governor of Yingzhou commandery.
value.literal: At first as householder to the heir apparent by accumulated transfers became Secretariat gentleman, went out as Inspector of You Province, governor of Yingzhou.

value.zh: 是時武帝置黃沙獄，以典詔囚。
value.en: At that time Emperor Wu founded the Yellow Sand prison for prisoners sentenced by imperial edict.
value.literal: At this time Emperor Wu established Yellow Sand prison, to manage edict prisoners.

value.zh: 以光曆世明法，用為黃沙御史，秩與中丞同，遷廷尉。
value.en: Because his family had long mastered the code, Guang was named censor of Yellow Sand with rank equal to the palace assistant secretary, then promoted director of justice.
value.literal: Because Guang through generations understood law, he was used as Yellow Sand censor; rank was the same as the palace assistant secretary; he was promoted Director of Justice.

value.zh: 元康中，拜尚書，典三公曹。
value.en: During Yuankang he was appointed minister of the masters of writing in charge of the Three Dukes section.
value.literal: In Yuankang he was appointed Minister of the Secretariat, in charge of the Three Dukes bureau.

value.zh: 時趙王倫篡逆，光於其際，守道全貞。
value.en: When Sima Lun, prince of Zhao, usurped the throne, Guang held to principle and kept his integrity intact.
value.literal: When Prince of Zhao Lun usurped and rebelled, Guang at that juncture kept the Way and preserved integrity.

value.zh: 及倫賜死，齊王冏輔政，復以光為廷尉，遷尚書，加奉車都尉。
value.en: After Lun was forced to take his life and Prince Jiong of Qi directed the government, Guang was again named director of justice, then minister of the masters of writing with the added title colonel who conducts the carriage.
value.literal: When Lun was ordered to die, Prince of Qi Jiong assisted governance; again they made Guang Director of Justice, promoted Minister of the Secretariat, added Colonel Who Conducts the Carriage.

value.zh: 後從駕討成都王穎有勳，封延陵縣公，邑千八百戶。
value.en: Later he accompanied the imperial train against Prince Ying of Chengdu and earned distinction; he was enfeoffed as duke of Yanling county with one thousand eight hundred households.
value.literal: Later following the carriage in punishing Prince of Chengdu Ying he had merit; he was enfeoffed duke of Yanling county, fief one thousand eight hundred households.

value.zh: 于時朝廷咸推光明于用法，故頻典理官。
value.en: The whole court acknowledged his clarity in applying the law, so he was repeatedly placed over the judiciary.
value.literal: At that time the court all pushed Guang as clear in applying law; therefore repeatedly he managed judicial offices.

value.zh: 惠帝為張方所逼，幸長安，朝臣奔散，莫有從者，光獨侍帝而西。
value.en: When Emperor Hui was driven by Zhang Fang to take refuge in Chang'an and the court fled in panic with none willing to follow, Guang alone accompanied the emperor westward.
value.literal: Emperor Hui was pressed by Zhang Fang, traveled to Chang'an; court ministers ran and scattered; none had followers; Guang alone attended the emperor going west.

value.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，加散騎常侍。
value.en: He was promoted left vice-director of the masters of writing with the added title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
value.literal: He was promoted Left Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

value.zh: 光兄誕為上官巳等所用，曆徐、雍二州刺史。
value.en: Guang's elder brother Dan was employed by Shangguan Si and his faction and served as inspector of Xu and Yong provinces in turn.
value.literal: Guang's elder brother Dan was used by Shangguan Si and others, successively was Inspector of Xu and Yong provinces.

value.zh: 誕性任放無倫次，而決烈過人，與光異操。
value.en: Dan was wild and unmethodical, yet bolder than most—a temper quite unlike his brother's.
value.literal: Dan's nature was unbridled and unrestrained without order, yet decisive and fierce surpassing others; with Guang his conduct differed.

value.zh: 常謂光小節，恆輕侮之，光事誕愈謹。
value.en: He constantly mocked Guang for fussiness and treated him with contempt, yet Guang served his elder brother with growing deference.
value.literal: He always called Guang petty scruples, constantly treated him lightly and insulted him; Guang serving Dan became more careful.

value.zh: 帝既還洛陽，時太弟新立，重選傅訓，以光為少傅，加光祿大夫，常侍如故。
value.en: After the emperor returned to Luoyang, the imperial younger brother had just been installed as heir and tutors were chosen with care; Guang was named junior tutor with the added title grand master of splendid carriage while keeping his post as attendant-in-ordinary.
value.literal: When the emperor had returned to Luoyang, at the time the imperial younger brother was newly established; heavily selecting tutors and instruction, they made Guang Junior Tutor, added Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, attendant-in-ordinary as before.

value.zh: 及懷帝即位，加光祿大夫金章紫綬，與傅祗並見推崇。
value.en: When Emperor Huai came to the throne, Guang received the grand master of splendid carriage's gold seal and purple ribbon and was honored together with Fu Zhi.
value.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended, he added Grand Master of Splendid Carriage gold seal purple ribbon, together with Fu Zhi both were seen honored and promoted.

value.zh: 尋為尚書令，本官如故。
value.en: Soon he was named director of the masters of writing while retaining his other titles.
value.literal: Shortly he became Director of the Masters of Writing; original offices as before.

value.zh: 以疾卒，贈司空、侍中。
value.en: He died of illness and was posthumously named minister of works and palace attendant.
value.literal: Because of illness he died; posthumously Minister of Works, Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 屬京洛傾覆，竟未加諡。
value.en: The fall of Luoyang followed so closely that no posthumous title was ever conferred.
value.literal: It fell when capital and Luoyang overturned; in the end no posthumous name was added.

value.zh: 傅玄
value.en: Fu Xuan
value.literal: Fu Xuan.

value.zh: 尋遷太子少傅，上章遜位還第。
value.en: Soon he became junior tutor to the heir apparent, then begged leave to retire home.
value.literal: Soon he was promoted junior tutor to the heir apparent; he submitted a memorial yielding office and returning home.

value.zh: 及成都王穎為太傅，復以祗為少傅，加侍中。
value.en: When Prince Chengdu Sima Ying became grand tutor, he again named Fu Zhi junior tutor with added palace attendant.
value.literal: When Prince Chengdu, Ying, was grand tutor, again he made Zhi junior tutor, added palace attendant.

value.zh: 懷帝即位，遷光祿大夫、侍中，未拜，加右僕射、中書監。
value.en: Under Emperor Huai he rose to grand counsellor of splendid horses and palace attendant, then—before the first appointment took effect—added right vice-director and overseer of the secretariat.
value.literal: When Emperor Huai mounted the throne, he was promoted grand counsellor of splendid horses and palace attendant; before investiture he was added right vice-director and overseer of the secretariat.

value.zh: 時太傅東海王越輔政，祗既居端右，每宣君臣謙光之道，由此上下雍穆。
value.en: While Grand Tutor Prince Donghai Sima Yue governed, Fu Zhi as senior minister on the right preached mutual deference between sovereign and ministers, and court relations grew calm.
value.literal: At that time grand tutor Prince of Donghai Yue directed the government; Zhi already stood at the head of the right—often he proclaimed the way of ruler and ministers yielding glory, and thereby above and below were harmonious and reverent.

value.zh: 祗明達國體，朝廷制度多所經綜。
value.en: He grasped how the state should run and had shaped many of its institutions.
value.literal: Zhi understood the state's body; many court systems he had managed and drawn together.

value.zh: 曆左光祿、開府，行太子太傅，侍中如故。
value.en: He passed through left grand master of splendid horses with independent establishment, acting grand tutor to the heir apparent, still a palace attendant.
value.literal: He served as left grand master of splendid horses, established office, acting grand tutor to the heir apparent, palace attendant as before.

value.zh: 疾篤遜位，不許。
value.en: Gravely ill, he asked to retire; the court refused.
value.literal: On grave illness he yielded office—not permitted.

value.zh: 遷司徒，以足疾，詔版輿上殿，不拜。
value.en: Raised to minister of education, he was carried in a litter to court because of his feet and excused from bowing.
value.literal: He was promoted minister of education; on foot ailment an edict ordered a litter to the hall; he did not bow.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃後之貴，不能假借之。
value.en: Yu refused to flatter Jia Mi.
value.literal: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.

value.zh: 謐至東宮，或舍之而於後庭遊戲。
value.en: He left Jia Mi cooling heels while he played inside.
value.literal: When Mi came to the Eastern Palace he sometimes left him waiting while he played in the inner courts.

value.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「賈謐甚有寵于中宮，而有不順之色，若一旦交構，大事去矣。
value.en: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: "Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.
value.literal: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: 'Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.

value.zh: 宜深自謙屈，以防其變，廣延賢士，用自輔翼。」
value.en: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings."
value.literal: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings.'

value.zh: 太子不能從。
value.en: Yu ignored him.
value.literal: The crown prince would not follow.

value.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。
value.en: Guo Huai once pushed a Han match—Yu wanted it too.
value.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.

value.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。
value.en: Jia Wu and the empress forced Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng instead.
value.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.

value.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。
value.en: Yu resented losing Wang's elder beauty to Jia Mi.
value.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.

value.zh: 謐嘗與太子圍棋，爭道，成都王穎見而訶謐，謐意愈不平，因此譖太子于後曰：「太子廣買田業，多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。
value.en: Once while playing go with the crown prince Mi quarreled over a move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: "The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
value.literal: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.

value.zh: 密聞其言云：'皇后萬歲後，吾當魚肉之。
value.en: Mi quoted Yu vowing to slaughter the Jias after Jia died.
value.literal: I have secretly heard him say: "After the empress dies, I shall butcher them."

value.zh: '非但如是也，若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等而廢後於金墉，如反手耳。
value.en: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.
value.literal: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.

value.zh: 不如早為之所，更立慈順者以自防衛。」
value.en: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves."
value.literal: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves.'

value.zh: 後納其言，又宣揚太子之短，布諸遠近。
value.en: Jia adopted the plot and smeared Yu empire-wide.
value.literal: The empress accepted his words and further broadcast the crown prince's faults throughout near and far.

value.zh: 于時朝野咸知賈后有害太子意。
value.en: Everyone saw Jia meant to kill the heir.
value.literal: Then court and countryside knew the empress meant to harm the crown prince.

value.zh: 中護軍趙俊請太子廢後，太子不聽。
value.en: Zhao Jun urged preemptive deposition—Yu declined.
value.literal: Central Guard Zhao Jun asked the crown prince to depose the empress first; the crown prince refused.

value.zh: 邵續
value.en: Shao Xu
value.literal: Shao Xu

value.zh: 邵續，字嗣祖，魏郡安陽人也。
value.en: Shao Xu, courtesy Sizu, came from Anyang in Wei Commandery.
value.literal: Shao Xu, style name Sizu, was a man of Anyang in Wei Commandery.

value.zh: 父乘，散騎侍郎。
value.en: His father, Shao Cheng, had risen to gentleman attendant at leisure.
value.literal: His father Shao Cheng was gentleman attendant at leisure.

value.zh: 續樸素有志烈，博覽經史，善談理義，妙解天文。
value.en: Shao Xu lived plainly and held fierce convictions; he read deeply across the classics and histories, argued principle with ease, and read the stars with uncommon skill.
value.literal: Shao Xu was plain and frugal and possessed of fierce resolve; he read widely in the classics and histories, was skilled at discussing principle and meaning, and had a subtle grasp of astronomy.

value.zh: 初為成都王穎參軍，穎將討長沙王乂，續諫曰：「續聞兄弟如左右手，今明公當天下之敵，而欲去一手乎？
value.en: He first joined the staff of Prince Chengdu, Sima Ying. When Ying prepared to strike Prince Changsha, Sima Yi, Shao Xu urged him: "They say brothers are like a man's two hands; you stand against the whole realm—would you willingly cut one off?
value.literal: At first he served as army adviser to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying; when Ying was about to campaign against Prince Changsha Sima Yi, Shao Xu remonstrated: "I have heard that brothers are like the left and right hand; now the enlightened lord faces the empire's foes—would you wish to remove one hand?

value.zh: 續竊惑之。」
value.en: He could not fathom Ying's plan."
value.literal: Shao Xu privately was perplexed by this."

value.zh: 穎不納。
value.en: Ying would not listen.
value.literal: Ying did not accept it.

value.zh: 後為苟晞參軍，除沁水令。
value.en: He later served on Gou Xi's staff and was named magistrate of Qinshui.
value.literal: Later he served as army adviser to Gou Xi and was appointed magistrate of Qinshui.

value.zh: 應詹字思遠，汝南南頓人，魏侍中璩之孫也。
value.en: Ying Zhan, whose courtesy name was Siyuan, came from Nandun in Runan; he was the grandson of Ying Qu, who had served Wei as Palace Attendant.
value.literal: Ying Zhan, courtesy name Siyuan, was a native of Nandun in Runan, and a grandson of Ying Qu, Palace Attendant of Wei.

value.zh: 詹幼孤，爲祖母所養。
value.en: He lost his parents while still a boy and was brought up by his grandmother.
value.literal: In youth he was orphaned and was raised by his grandmother.

value.zh: 年十餘歲，祖母又終，居喪毀頓，杖而後起，遂以孝聞。
value.en: After his grandmother died when he was just past ten, he mourned until his body gave way and he needed a walking stick to stand; word of his filial piety spread.
value.literal: When he was a little over ten sui, his grandmother also died; in mourning he wasted away so badly that he could rise only with a staff, and he came to be known for his filial devotion.

value.zh: 家富於財，年又稚弱，乃請族人共居，委以資產，情若至親，世以此異焉。
value.en: The family was wealthy, but he was still a child; he asked his kinsmen to share one roof with him and handed his assets into their care, treating them as his nearest kin—an act that struck people of the time as extraordinary.
value.literal: His household was rich in wealth, and he was still very young, so he invited his clansmen to live together with him, entrusting them with his property; their feelings were like those of the closest kin, and the world marveled at this on that account.

value.zh: 弱冠知名，性質素弘雅，物雖犯而弗之校，以學藝文章稱。
value.en: After his capping he won a reputation; he was steady, broad-minded, and elegant by temperament, slow to take offense when others crossed him, and admired for his scholarship, arts, and writing.
value.literal: At the capping age he was already well known; by nature he was plain, magnanimous, and refined, and though things might offend him he did not contend with them; he was esteemed for learning, craft, and literary skill.

value.zh: 司徒何劭見之曰：「君子哉若人！」
value.en: When Situ He Shao met him, he exclaimed, “Here is a true gentleman.”
value.literal: Situ He Shao, seeing him, said, “What a gentleman this man is!”

value.zh: 初辟公府，爲太子舍人。
value.en: He first received appointment from the general administration and served as Gentleman Attendant of the heir apparent.
value.literal: At first he was summoned to office from the princely administration and became Attendant to the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 趙王倫以爲征東長史。
value.en: Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, named him senior clerk on the staff of the eastward expedition.
value.literal: The Prince of Zhao, Sima Lun, appointed him Senior Clerk of the East Expedition.

value.zh: 倫誅，坐免。
value.en: After Sima Lun was put to death, Ying Zhan was stripped of office by association.
value.literal: When Lun was executed, he was implicated and dismissed.

value.zh: 成都王穎辟爲掾。
value.en: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, recruited him to his secretariat.
value.literal: The Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, summoned him as a retainer.

value.zh: 時驃騎從事中郎諸葛玫委長沙王乂奔鄴，盛稱乂之非。
value.en: At the time Zhuge Mei, who served as clerk on the dashing cavalry general’s staff, had left Prince Sima Yi of Changsha for Ye and was loudly blackening Yi’s name.
value.literal: At that time Zhuge Mei, Attendant Clerk on the staff of the Cavalry-in-Attendant, had abandoned Prince Sima Yi of Changsha and fled to Ye, loudly denouncing Yi’s faults.

value.zh: 玫浮躁有才辯，臨漳人士無不詣之。
value.en: Zhuge Mei was volatile yet eloquent, and everyone of standing around Linzhang beat a path to his door.
value.literal: Mei was restless and sharp-tongued; there was not a person of note in Linzhang who did not go to call on him.

value.zh: 詹與玫有舊，歎曰：「諸葛仁林何與樂毅之相詭乎！」
value.en: Zhan had known Zhuge Mei for years and sighed, “How can Zhuge Renlin diverge so wildly from the conduct of Yue Yi!”
value.literal: Zhan had old ties with Mei and sighed, saying, “How can Renlin of the Zhuge clan be so unlike the way Yue Yi comported himself!”

value.zh: 卒不見之。
value.en: He never went to see him.
value.literal: In the end he did not go to see him.

value.zh: 玫聞甚愧。
value.en: When Zhuge Mei heard, he was mortified.
value.literal: When Mei heard of this he was deeply ashamed.

value.zh: 鎮南大將軍劉弘，詹之祖舅也，請爲長史，謂之曰：「君器識弘深，後當代老子於荊南矣。」
value.en: Liu Hong, General Who Guards the South and Zhan’s grandfather on his mother’s side, invited him as senior clerk and told him, “Your talent and judgment run deep; in time you will succeed me in holding the Jing southlands.”
value.literal: General Who Guards the South, Liu Hong—Zhan’s maternal grandfather—asked him to serve as senior clerk and said to him, “Your capacity and insight are broad and deep; one day you will take this old man’s place south of the Jing region.”

value.zh: 仍委以軍政。
value.en: He then placed military affairs in his hands.
value.literal: Thereupon he entrusted him with military administration.

value.zh: 弘著績漢南，詹之力也。
value.en: Liu Hong’s record of achievement in the southern Han basin owed much to Ying Zhan’s exertions.
value.literal: Hong achieved merit south of the Han, and it was through Zhan’s efforts.

value.zh: 遷南平太守。
value.en: He rose to become administrator of Nanping commandery.
value.literal: He was promoted to Administrator of Nanping.

value.zh: 孫惠
value.en: Sun Hui.
value.literal: Section heading: Sun Hui.

value.zh: 孫惠，字德施，吳國富陽人，吳豫章太守賁曾孫也。
value.en: Sun Hui, whose courtesy name was Deshi, came from Fuyang in the old state of Wu and was a great-grandson of Ben, the Yuzhang grand administrator who had served Wu.
value.literal: Sun Hui, courtesy name Deshi, was a native of Fuyang in the state of Wu; he was a great-grandson of Ben, who had been Grand Administrator of Yuzhang under Wu.

value.zh: 父祖並仕吳。
value.en: Both his father and his grandfather had served the Wu regime.
value.literal: His father and grandfather both held office in Wu.

value.zh: 惠口訥，好學有才識，州辟不就，寓居蕭沛之間。
value.en: He was awkward in speech but a devoted student, with real ability and insight. Though the provincial authorities tried to appoint him, he stayed out of office and lived for a time between Xiao and Pei.
value.literal: Hui was slow of tongue, loved learning, and had talent and judgment; the province summoned him but he did not take office, and he lodged between Xiao and Pei.

value.zh: 永甯初，赴齊王冏義，討趙王倫，以功封晉興縣侯，辟大司馬戶曹掾，轉東曹屬。
value.en: When Yongning began, he joined Sima Jiong, the Prince of Qi, in the loyalist campaign against Sima Lun, the Prince of Zhao. His service earned him the county marquisate of Jinxing, a post as clerk in the minister of war's revenue office, and then a place on the eastern staff.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Yongning era, he answered Prince of Qi Jiong's call to righteous arms and campaigned against Prince of Zhao Lun; for merit he was enfeoffed marquis of Jinxing County, appointed clerk in the Revenue Bureau of the Minister of War, then transferred to a subordinate post in the eastern bureau.

value.zh: 冏驕矜僭侈，天下失望。
value.en: Jiong grew haughty and overbearing, overstepping his rank and spending on a princely scale until the empire had lost faith in him.
value.literal: Jiong was arrogant, boastful, presumptuous, and extravagant; all under Heaven were disappointed in him.

value.zh: 惠獻言於冏，諷以五難、四不可，勸令歸籓，辭甚切至。
value.en: Sun Hui laid before him a carefully framed remonstrance—the 'five difficulties' and 'four impossibilities'—urging him to withdraw to his princely domain. The tone was urgent and uncompromising.
value.literal: Hui submitted advice to Jiong, using 'five difficulties' and 'four impossibilities' as indirect admonition, urging him to return to his fief; the wording was extremely blunt and thorough.

value.zh: 冏不納。
value.en: Jiong refused to listen.
value.literal: Jiong did not accept it.

value.zh: 惠懼罪，辭疾去。
value.en: Fearing reprisals, Sun Hui pleaded illness and slipped away.
value.literal: Hui feared punishment, pleaded illness, and departed.

value.zh: 頃之，冏果敗。
value.en: Soon afterward Jiong fell, exactly as he had warned.
value.literal: Before long, Jiong indeed was defeated.

value.zh: 成都王穎薦惠為大將軍參軍、領奮威將軍、白沙督。
value.en: Sima Ying, the Prince of Chengdu, then recommended him as an adviser on the grand general's staff, with the concurrent titles of General Who Rouses Might and commander of the Baisha garrison.
value.literal: Prince of Chengdu Ying recommended Hui as staff adviser to the grand general, concurrently General Who Rouses Might, and commander at Baisha.

value.zh: 是時，穎將征長沙王乂，以陸機為前鋒都督。
value.en: Ying was preparing to move against Sima Yi, the Prince of Changsha, and named Lu Ji to lead the van.
value.literal: At this time Ying was about to campaign against Prince of Changsha Yi and appointed Lu Ji as commander of the vanguard.

value.zh: 惠與機同鄉里，憂其致禍，勸機讓都督于王粹。
value.en: As a townsman of Lu Ji, Sun Hui worried the appointment would destroy him and urged him to step aside in favor of Wang Cui.
value.literal: Hui was from the same home region as Ji; fearing that Ji would bring disaster on himself, he urged Ji to yield the commander's post to Wang Cui.

value.zh: 及機兄弟被戮，惠甚傷恨之。
value.en: When Lu Ji and his brothers were put to death, Sun Hui mourned them bitterly.
value.literal: When Ji and his brothers were executed, Hui deeply grieved and resented it.

value.zh: 時惠又擅殺穎牙門將梁俊，懼罪，因改姓名以遁。
value.en: He had already killed Liang Jun, one of Ying's gate generals, without orders. Dreading the consequences, he took a new identity and went into hiding.
value.literal: At that time Hui had also on his own authority killed Liang Jun, a gate-guard general under Ying; fearing punishment, he changed his name and fled into hiding.

value.zh: 序
value.en: Preface
value.literal: Preface

value.zh: 趙王倫篡位，署為侍中。
value.en: When Prince of Zhao Sima Lun seized the throne, Shao was named Palace Attendant.
value.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne, Shao was appointed Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 惠帝復阼，遂居其職。
value.en: After Emperor Hui was restored, Shao kept the same office.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui resumed the throne, Shao remained in that role.

value.zh: 司空張華為倫所誅，議者追理其事，欲復其爵，紹又駁曰：「臣之事君，當除煩去惑。
value.en: When Minister of Works Zhang Hua was put to death by Lun, some argued for restoring his titles; Shao objected again: "A minister's duty is to clear away trouble and delusion for his sovereign.
value.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Hua was executed by Lun; debaters revisited the matter and wished to restore his noble rank, but Shao again objected: "A minister serves his lord by removing confusion and distraction.

value.zh: 華歷位內外，雖粗有善事，然闔棺之責，著於遠近，兆禍始亂，華實為之。
value.en: Zhang Hua moved between palace and camp and did some good in small ways, yet his final reckoning was visible everywhere: the seeds of disaster were largely of his planting.
value.literal: Hua held posts inside and outside the court; though he had some decent deeds, the blame that closes the coffin was plain far and near—the omens that began the calamity were really his doing.

value.zh: 故鄭討幽公之亂，斫子家之棺；
value.en: So Zheng, punishing Duke You of Lu's rebellion, split minister Zijia's coffin open with an axe.
value.literal: Hence when Zheng punished the turmoil of Duke You, they hacked open Zijia's coffin;

value.zh: 魯戮隱罪，終篇貶翬。
value.en: Lu executed Guan Yin for his crime, and the Spring and Autumn closes by censuring Hui.
value.literal: Lu executed Yin for his guilt, and the classic ends by censuring Hui.

value.zh: 未忍重戮，事已弘矣，謂不宜復其爵位，理其無罪。」
value.en: I will not press for harsher punishment than death; the case is already settled. Restoring his titles or declaring him blameless would be wrong."
value.literal: I cannot bear to urge heavier punishment; the matter is already broad enough—I say his rank should not be restored nor his innocence proclaimed."

value.zh: 時帝初反正，紹又上疏曰：「臣聞改前轍者則車不傾，革往弊者則政不爽。
value.en: With the emperor newly restored, Shao submitted another memorial: "They say that straightening the wheel tracks keeps the carriage upright, and curing old abuses keeps government true.
value.literal: At the time the emperor had just been restored; Shao further submitted a memorial: "I have heard that those who correct the rut keep the cart from tipping; those who mend past abuses keep government sound.

value.zh: 太一統于元首，百司役於多士，故周文興于上，成康穆於下也。
value.en: The supreme pivot sits with the ruler; every ministry depends on capable men—thus King Wen flourished on high while kings Cheng and Kang enjoyed peace below.
value.literal: The Grand Unity rests in the sovereign's head; myriad offices labor through many officers—thus King Wen rose above and Cheng and Kang were tranquil below.

value.zh: 存不忘亡，《易》之善義；
value.en: The Changes teaches us to remember peril even in safety—
value.literal: To remember survival amid peril is the fine meaning of the Changes;

value.zh: 願陛下無忘金墉，大司馬無忘潁上，大將軍無忘黃橋，則禍亂之萌無由而兆矣。」
value.en: May Your Majesty remember the fortress at Jinyong; may the Grand Marshal remember Yingshang; may the Grand General remember Huang Bridge—then the seeds of calamity will never sprout."
value.literal: I pray Your Majesty will not forget Jinyong; the Grand Marshal will not forget Yingshang; the Grand General will not forget Huang Bridge—then the sprouts of disaster will have nowhere to arise."

value.zh: 尋徵為御史中丞，未拜，復為侍中。
value.en: He was soon summoned as assistant chief of the Censorate but, before taking up the post, was again named Palace Attendant.
value.literal: Soon he was summoned as Palace Assistant Clerk of the Censorate; before he took office he again became Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 河間王顒、成都王穎舉兵向京都，以討長沙王乂，大駕次於城東。
value.en: Prince of Hejian Sima Yong and Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying marched on the capital against Prince of Changsha Sima Yi; the imperial train halted east of the walls.
value.literal: Prince of Hejian Sima Yong and Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying raised troops toward the capital to strike Prince of Changsha Sima Yi; the imperial carriage halted east of the city.

value.zh: 乂言於眾曰：「今日西討，欲誰為都督乎？」
value.en: Yi asked the gathered officers: "For this western campaign, whom do you want as overall commander?"
value.literal: Yi said to the assembly: "Today we march west—whom do you wish as commander?"

value.zh: 六軍之士皆曰：「願嵇侍中戮力前驅，死猶生也。」
value.en: The men of the six armies shouted: "We want Palace Attendant Ji in the van—we would rather die beside him than live elsewhere!"
value.literal: The troops of the six armies said: "We wish Palace Attendant Ji to strain every nerve in the vanguard—to die would be as living."

value.zh: 遂拜紹使持節、平西將軍。
value.en: So Shao received the credential-bearing commission and the title General Who Pacifies the West.
value.literal: Shao was therefore appointed commissioner bearing credentials and General Who Pacifies the West.

value.zh: 屬乂被執，紹復為侍中。
value.en: After Yi was captured, Shao returned to the post of Palace Attendant.
value.literal: When Yi was seized, Shao again became Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 公王以下皆詣鄴謝罪於穎，紹等咸見廢黜，免為庶人。
value.en: Every prince and noble went to Ye to submit to Sima Ying; Shao and his peers were stripped of office and reduced to common status.
value.literal: All ranks from dukes and princes downward went to Ye to apologize to Ying; Shao and others were all cashiered and reduced to commoners.

value.zh: 尋而朝廷復有北征之役，征紹，復其爵位。
value.en: Soon the court launched another northern campaign, recalled Shao, and restored his titles.
value.literal: Soon the court mounted another northern expedition and summoned Shao, restoring his noble rank.

value.zh: 紹以天子蒙塵，承詔馳詣行在所。
value.en: With the emperor on the run, Shao took the edict and rode hard for the imperial headquarters.
value.literal: Because the Son of Heaven was in exile, Shao received the edict and galloped to the temporary residence.

value.zh: 值王師敗績于蕩陰，百官及侍衛莫不散潰，唯紹儼然端冕，以身捍衛，兵交御輦，飛箭雨集，紹遂被害於帝側，血濺御服，天子深哀歎之。
value.en: At Dangyin the imperial army collapsed; ministers and guards fled—only Shao, erect in full court dress, threw himself between the emperor and the blades. Weapons clashed around the carriage, arrows fell like rain, and Shao died at the sovereign's side, his blood staining the imperial robe while the emperor wept over him.
value.literal: When the royal army was routed at Dangyin, officials and guards scattered in panic—only Shao, unmoved in full court garb, shielded the ruler with his body; weapons clashed about the imperial carriage and arrows fell like rain; Shao was thus slain beside the emperor, his blood splashing the imperial robe, and the Son of Heaven mourned him deeply.

value.zh: 及事定，左右欲浣衣，帝曰：「此嵇侍中血，勿去。」
value.en: Afterward, servants wanted to launder the robe; the emperor said: "That is Palace Attendant Ji's blood—leave it."
value.literal: When things settled, attendants wished to wash the robe; the emperor said: "This is Palace Attendant Ji's blood—do not remove it."

value.zh: 齊王冏辟為征西參軍，襲爵武昌鄉侯。
value.en: Prince of Qi Sima Jiong appointed him adjutant on the western campaign, and he inherited the village marquisate at Wuchang.
value.literal: Prince of Qi Sima Jiong summoned him as adjutant on the western expedition and he inherited the village marquisate of Wuchang.

value.zh: 長沙王乂召為驃騎記室督、尚書郎。
value.en: Prince of Changsha Sima Yi appointed him recorder-in-chief to the chief commander and Gentleman of the Secretariat.
value.literal: Prince of Changsha Sima Yi summoned him as recorder-in-chief to the chief commander and Gentleman of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 乂與成都王穎交戰，穎軍轉盛，尚書郎旦出督戰，夜還理事。
value.en: When Yi clashed with Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying, Ying's forces gained ground; the Secretariat gentlemen rode out at dawn to supervise the fighting and returned after dark to manage paperwork.
value.literal: Yi fought Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying; Ying's army grew stronger; the Secretariat gentlemen went out at dawn to oversee battle and returned at night to handle affairs.

value.zh: 含言於乂曰：「昔魏武每有軍事，增置掾屬。
value.en: Han urged Yi: "Whenever Emperor Wu of Wei faced war, he expanded aide posts.
value.literal: Han said to Yi: "In old days whenever Wu of Wei had military affairs, he added aides and staff.

value.zh: 青龍二年，尚書令陳矯以有軍務，亦奏增郎。
value.en: In Qinglong 2, Director of the Secretariat Chen Jiao, citing military business, likewise petitioned for added Secretariat gentlemen.
value.literal: In the second year of Qinglong, Director of the Secretariat Chen Jiao, because there were military matters, also memorialized to add gentlemen.

value.zh: 今奸逆四逼，王路擁塞，倒懸之急，不復過此。
value.en: Today rebels ring us on every side; the imperial highways clog; we hang by our heels—nothing could be more urgent.
value.literal: Now treason presses from four sides; the royal road is blocked; the urgency of hanging upside down could not be greater.

value.zh: 但居曹理事，尚須增郎，況今都官中騎三曹晝出督戰，夜還理事，一人兩役，內外廢乏。
value.en: Stationery offices still need extra hands in quiet times—how much more when the Capital, Palace, and Cavalry sections march out by day to direct combat and draft orders by night; one officer pulling double duty exhausts both camp and capital.
value.literal: Yet merely sitting in headquarters handling business still requires added gentlemen—how much more now when the Capital Bureau, Palace Bureau, and Cavalry Bureau go out by day to oversee battle and return by night to handle affairs—one man bearing two duties, inner and outer alike exhausted.

value.zh: 含謂今有十萬人，都督各有主帥，推轂授綏，委付大將，不宜復令台僚雜與其間。」
value.en: Han argues that with a hundred thousand troops under distinct commanders—each lieutenant invested with drum and reins—a chief general should hold the line; secretariat aides ought not clutter the chain of command."
value.literal: Han holds that with one hundred thousand men, each command has its commander; push the carriage and hand the reins—entrust it to a great general; you should not again let terrace aides mix among them."

value.zh: 乂從之，乃增郎及令史。
value.en: Yi agreed and expanded the Secretariat rolls with added gentlemen and clerks.
value.literal: Yi followed him and added gentlemen and clerks.

value.zh: 王育，字伯春，京兆人也。
value.en: Wang Yu, courtesy name Bochun, hailed from Jingzhao.
value.literal: Wang Yu, courtesy name Bochun, was a man of Jingzhao.

value.zh: 少孤貧，為人傭牧羊，每過小學，必歔欷流涕。
value.en: Poor and orphaned early, he hired out as a shepherd—passing village schools he always wept.
value.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he hired out shepherding sheep for others; whenever he passed a village school he always sobbed and shed tears.

value.zh: 時有暇，即折蒲學書，忘而失羊，為羊主所責，育將鬻己以償之。
value.en: He stole moments to scratch letters on rushes—lost sheep and faced his master's wrath—ready to sell himself to pay.
value.literal: When he had spare time he broke rushes to practice writing—forgetting and losing sheep—blamed by the sheep owner; Yu was about to sell himself to compensate.

value.zh: 同郡許子章，敏達之士也，聞而嘉之，代育償羊，給其衣食，使與子同學，遂博通經史。
value.en: Xu Zizhang of the same commandery, a generous scholar, paid his debt, clothed and fed him, and enrolled him beside his sons until Yu mastered the canon.
value.literal: Xu Zizhang of the same commandery, a keen and accomplished man, heard and praised him; he compensated Yu's sheep for him and supplied clothes and food, had him study with his sons—thereupon Yu broadly mastered classics and histories.

value.zh: 身長八尺餘，須長三尺，容貌絕異，音聲動人。
value.en: He stood over eight chi tall with a three-chi beard—features unforgettable, voice compelling.
value.literal: His height exceeded eight chi; his beard was three chi; his appearance was strikingly unusual; his voice moved others.

value.zh: 子章以兄之子妻之，為立別宅，分之資業，育受之無愧色。
value.en: Zizhang married a niece to him, built him a house, and split property—Yu accepted without false modesty.
value.literal: Zizhang married his elder brother's daughter to him, built him a separate residence, and divided property with him—Yu accepted without shame.

value.zh: 然行己任性，頗不偶俗。
value.en: Yet he followed his own bent and ignored fashionable manners.
value.literal: Yet in conduct he indulged his nature and largely did not conform to common ways.

value.zh: 妻喪，吊之者不過四五人，然皆鄉閭名士。
value.en: Only four or five mourners attended his wife's funeral—all were local worthies.
value.literal: At his wife's funeral only four or five mourners came—yet all were eminent men of village and lane.

value.zh: 太守杜宣命為主簿。
value.en: Prefect Du Xuan named him chief clerk.
value.literal: Administrator Du Xuan appointed him chief clerk.

value.zh: 俄而宣左遷萬年令，杜令王攸詣宣，宣不迎之，攸怒曰：「卿往為二千石，吾所敬也。
value.en: Soon Du Xuan became magistrate of Wannian; Wang You of Duling visited—Xuan refused a reception—You snapped: "You once ranked two thousand shi—I honored you.
value.literal: Shortly Xuan was transferred down to magistrate of Wannian; Magistrate Wang You called on Xuan—Xuan did not go out to welcome him; You angrily said: "You formerly held two thousand shi—we respected you.

value.zh: 今吾儕耳，何故不見迎？
value.en: We are equals now—why no welcome?
value.literal: Now we are peers—why do you not come welcome me?

value.zh: 欲以小雀遇我，使我畏死鷂乎？」
value.en: Do you treat me like a sparrow and expect terror before your goshawk?"
value.literal: Do you mean to treat me like a little sparrow and make me fear a death hawk?"

value.zh: 育執刀叱攸曰：「君辱臣死，自昔而然。
value.en: Wang Yu drew a blade and roared at Magistrate You: "When the master is shamed, his man must die—the rule is ancient.
value.literal: Wang Yu seized a knife and shouted at You: "When the lord is insulted the minister dies—it has been so since antiquity.

value.zh: 我府君以非罪黜降，如日月之蝕耳，小縣令敢輕辱吾君！
value.en: Our prefect fell without guilt—like a passing eclipse—how dare a county clerk insult him!
value.literal: Our prefect was dismissed without crime—like an eclipse of sun or moon—how dare a petty county magistrate lightly insult our lord!

value.zh: 汝謂吾刀鈍邪，敢如是乎！」
value.en: You think this blade dull—how dare you!"
value.literal: Do you say my blade is dull—how dare you behave thus!"

value.zh: 前將殺之。
value.en: He pressed forward to strike.
value.literal: He stepped forward to kill him.

value.zh: 宣懼，跣下抱育，乃止。
value.en: Xuan sprang barefoot to hug him still.
value.literal: Xuan feared, slipped barefoot down and embraced Yu—only then stopped.

value.zh: 自此知名。
value.en: His name spread from that day.
value.literal: From this he became known.

value.zh: 司徒王渾辟為掾，除南武陽令。
value.en: Minister of Works Wang Hun took him as aide, then named him magistrate of Nanwuyang.
value.literal: Minister of Works Wang Hun summoned him as aide; he was appointed magistrate of Nanwuyang.

value.zh: 為政清約，宿盜逃奔他郡。
value.en: His rule was spare and clean—veteran bandits fled to other counties.
value.literal: His governance was clear and restrained—long-standing bandits fled to other commanderies.

value.zh: 遷并州督護。
value.en: He rose to Bing Province supervisor.
value.literal: He was promoted to supervisor of Bing Province.

value.zh: 成都王穎在鄴，又以育為振武將軍。
value.en: Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying, camped at Ye, added the title General Who Rouses Might.
value.literal: Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying was at Ye and again made Yu General Who Rouses Might.

value.zh: 劉元海之為北單于，育說穎曰：「元海今去，育請為殿下促之，不然，懼不至也。」
value.en: When Liu Yuan became Northern Chanyu, Yu urged Ying: "Let me ride after him now or he may never come."
value.literal: When Liu Yuan became Northern Chanyu, Yu urged Ying: "Yuan is departing now—I beg to hurry him for Your Highness—otherwise I fear he will not come."

value.zh: 穎然之，以育為破虜將軍。
value.en: Ying agreed and named him General Who Breaks the Caitiffs.
value.literal: Ying agreed and made Yu General Who Breaks the Caitiffs.

value.zh: 元海遂拘之，其後以為太傅。
value.en: Liu Yuan seized him—later raised him to Grand Tutor.
value.literal: Yuan then detained him; afterward appointed him Grand Tutor.

value.zh: 序
value.en: Preface
value.literal: Preface

value.zh: 毗字長基。
value.en: Du Pi, courtesy Changji.
value.literal: Pi, courtesy name Changji.

value.zh: 州舉秀才，成都王穎辟大將軍掾，遷尚書郎，參太傅軍事。
value.en: Recommended as a cultivated talent, he entered Prince Chengdu Sima Ying's staff as grand-general aide, then became gentleman of the Masters of Writing and adviser on the grand tutor's army council.
value.literal: The province raised him as cultivated talent; Prince Chengdu Sima Ying summoned him as aide to the grand general; he was promoted Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and joined the Grand Tutor's military staff.

value.zh: 及洛陽覆沒，毗南渡江，王敦表為益州刺史，將與宜都太守柳純共固白帝。
value.en: After the Luoyang catastrophe he fled south; Wang Dun nominated him for Yi Province so he could join Yidu prefect Liu Chun in holding Baidi.
value.literal: When Luoyang fell he crossed south of the Yangzi; Wang Dun recommended him as Inspector of Yi Province; he was to cooperate with Administrator of Yidu Liu Chun in holding Ba Di.

value.zh: 杜弢遣軍要毗，遂遇害。
value.en: The rebel Du Tao ambushed him and cut him down.
value.literal: Du Tao sent troops to intercept Pi; Pi was killed.

value.zh: 軫弟烈，明政事，察孝廉，曆平康、安陽令，所居有異績，遷衡陽太守。
value.en: Du Lie, another brother of Du Zhen, excelled at governance; as filial-and-incorrupt nominee he magistrated Pingkang and Anyang with distinction, then became prefect of Hengyang.
value.literal: Zhen's younger brother Lie understood practical administration; recommended as filial and incorrupt, he served as magistrate of Pingkang and Anyang with outstanding records at each post; promoted Administrator of Hengyang.

value.zh: 聞軫亡，因自表兄子幼弱，求去官，詔轉犍為太守，蜀土榮之。
value.en: Learning of Du Zhen's death, he asked leave on the ground that his nephews were infants; the court moved him to Qianwei instead, a gesture Shu folk deeply respected.
value.literal: When he heard of Zhen's death he memorialized that his elder brother's sons were still young and weak and begged to resign; an edict transferred him to Administrator of Qianwei; the people of Shu honored him for it.

value.zh: 後遷湘東太守，為成都王穎郎中令，病卒。
value.en: He later governed Xiangdong and served as Chamberlain of the Palace Gentlemen to Prince Chengdu, then died of illness.
value.literal: Later promoted Administrator of Xiangdong, he served as Chamberlain of the Palace Attendants (langzhongling) to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying; died of illness.

value.zh: 喬智明，字元達，鮮卑前部人也。
value.en: Qiao Zhiming (courtesy Yuanda) belonged to the forward wing of the Xianbei confederation.
value.literal: Qiao Zhiming, courtesy name Yuanda, was a man of the forward division of the Xianbei.

value.zh: 少喪二親，哀毀過禮，長而以德行著稱。
value.en: Orphaned young, he mourned beyond ritual and matured renowned for character.
value.literal: In youth he lost both parents; his grief exceeded ritual propriety; grown, he was famed for virtuous conduct.

value.zh: 成都王穎辟為輔國將軍。
value.en: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying appointed him General Who Supports the State.
value.literal: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying summoned him as General Who Supports the State.

value.zh: 穎之敗趙王倫也，表智明為殄寇將軍、隆慮、共二縣令。
value.en: After defeating Prince Zhao Sima Lun, Sima Ying named him General Who Exterminates Brigands and magistrate of Longlu and Gong.
value.literal: When Ying defeated Prince Zhao Sima Lun, he memorialized Zhiming as General Who Exterminates Brigands and magistrate of Longlu and Gong counties.

value.zh: 二縣愛之，號為「神君」。
value.en: Both counties loved him; they called him the "divine magistrate."
value.literal: Both counties loved him; they called him the "divine magistrate."

value.zh: 部人張兌為父報仇，母老單身，有妻無子，智明湣之，停其獄。
value.en: Commoner Zhang Dui killed for vengeance; his mother lived alone and he lacked an heir; Qiao Zhiming stayed judgment out of mercy.
value.literal: A local man Zhang Dui avenged his father; his mother was old and lived alone; he had a wife but no son; Zhiming pitied him and stayed the case.

value.zh: 歲餘，令兌將妻入獄，兼陰縱之。
value.en: After a year he let Zhang bring his wife into custody and quietly allowed intimacy.
value.literal: After more than a year he ordered Dui to bring his wife into jail and secretly allowed conjugal visits.

value.zh: 人有勸兌逃者，兌曰：「有君如此，吾何忍累之！
value.en: Someone urged Dui to flee; Dui said: "With a magistrate like this, how could I bear to drag him down!
value.literal: Someone urged Dui to flee; Dui said: "With a magistrate like this, how could I bear to drag him down!

value.zh: 縱吾得免，作何面目視息世間！」
value.en: Even if I could escape, what face would I have to face the world and breathe!"
value.literal: Even if I could escape, what face would I have to face the world and breathe!"

value.zh: 於獄產一男。
value.en: His wife delivered a son in prison.
value.literal: In the jail his wife bore a boy.

value.zh: 會赦，得免。
value.en: An amnesty freed him.
value.literal: An amnesty arrived and he obtained release.

value.zh: 其仁感如是。
value.en: Such was the power of his humane rule.
value.literal: His humane kindness moved people thus.

value.zh: 惠帝之伐鄴也，穎以智明為折沖將軍、參丞相前鋒軍事。
value.en: During Emperor Hui's expedition against Ye, Sima Ying made him General Who Charges the Enemy on the vanguard staff.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui campaigned against Ye, Ying appointed Zhiming General Who Charges the Enemy and adjutant on the prime minister's vanguard staff.

value.zh: 智明勸穎奉迎乘輿，穎大怒曰：「卿名曉事，投身事孤。
value.en: Zhiming urged Ying to welcome the emperor's carriage; Ying raged: "Your reputation says you understand affairs—yet you entered my service.
value.literal: Zhiming urged Ying to welcome the emperor's carriage; Ying raged: "Your reputation says you understand affairs—yet you entered my service.

value.zh: 主上為群小所逼，將加非罪於孤，卿奈何欲使孤束手就刑邪！
value.en: The sovereign was forced by petty men and will heap false crimes on me—why would you have me bind my hands for execution!
value.literal: The sovereign was forced by petty men and will heap false crimes on me—why would you have me bind my hands for execution!

value.zh: 共事之義，正若此乎？」
value.en: Is comradeship supposed to mean this?"
value.literal: Is comradeship supposed to mean this?"

value.zh: 智明乃止。
value.en: Qiao Zhiming fell silent.
value.literal: Zhiming thereupon desisted.

value.zh: 尋屬永嘉之亂，仕于劉曜。
value.en: When Yongjia chaos erupted he entered Liu Yao's Han-Zhao regime.
value.literal: Soon the Yongjia turmoil came; he served Liu Yao.

value.zh: 詳觀往誥，逖聽前聞，階緣外戚以致顯榮者，其所由來尚矣。
value.en: A close reading of past injunctions and the lessons of earlier ages shows that riding kinship with the imperial consorts to wealth and rank is an old story.
value.literal: Carefully examining the admonitions of old and heeding what was heard in former times, those who climbed by ties to imperial affines to reach high honor—their origins go back a long way.

value.zh: 而多至禍敗，鮮克令終者，何哉？
value.en: Yet so many of them end in ruin, and precious few die in peace. Why is that?
value.literal: Yet many come to disaster and ruin, and few achieve a good end—why?

value.zh: 豈不由祿以恩升，位非德舉；
value.en: Surely it is because their salaries come from imperial favor rather than merit, and their posts are not won by moral weight.
value.literal: Is it not because emolument rises through favor, and office is not raised up by virtue?

value.zh: 識慚明悊。
value.en: Their judgment cannot bear comparison with true sagacity.
value.literal: In insight they are ashamed before clear wisdom.

value.zh: 材謝經通；
value.en: Their abilities fall short of real command of the canon.
value.literal: In talent they decline short of mastery of the classics.

value.zh: 假椒房之寵靈，總軍國之樞要。
value.en: They lean on the consort’s favor to seize the levers of military and civil power.
value.literal: Borrowing the favor and numinous power of the harem, they grasp the pivot of both army and state.

value.zh: 或威權震主，或勢力傾朝；
value.en: Some overshadow the throne; others bend the entire bureaucracy to their will.
value.literal: Some awe the ruler with their might and authority; some tilt the whole court with their power and influence.

value.zh: 居安而不慮危，務進而不知退；
value.en: They bask in ease and ignore danger; they press always forward and never learn when to step back.
value.literal: Dwelling in safety they do not think of peril; striving to advance they do not know to withdraw.

value.zh: 驕奢既至，釁隙隨之者乎！
value.en: Arrogance and excess invite their own undoing—is that not how the cracks appear?
value.literal: Once arrogance and extravagance have arrived, do breach and rift not follow!

value.zh: 是以呂霍之家，誅夷于西漢，梁鄧之族，剿絕於東都，其餘干紀亂常、害時蠹政者，不可勝載。
value.en: Hence the Lü and Huo lines were slaughtered in Western Han, and the Liang and Deng families extirpated at Luoyang; the roll of affines who broke the law, subverted custom, and poisoned the state would fill volumes.
value.literal: Therefore the houses of Lü and Huo were exterminated in Western Han; the clans of Liang and Deng were cut off in the Eastern capital; as for the rest who violated the norm, threw order into chaos, harmed the age, and worm-eaten governance—they cannot all be recorded.

value.zh: 至若樊靡卿之父子，竇廣國之弟兄，陰興之守約戒奢，史丹之掩惡揚善，斯並后族之所美者也。
value.en: Then there are the shining exceptions: Fan Miqing and his father, Dou Guangguo and his brothers, Yin Xing with his frugality and discipline, Shi Dan who muted scandal and lifted virtue—all models among imperial in-laws.
value.literal: As for Fan Miqing’s father and son, Dou Guangguo’s brothers, Yin Xing’s keeping restraint and warning against extravagance, and Shi Dan’s covering evil and proclaiming good—these are what the empress’s kin have to praise.

value.zh: 由此觀之，干時縱溢者必以凶終，守道謙沖者永保貞吉，古人所謂禍福無門，惟人所召，此非其效歟！
value.en: From this it is plain: those who ride the moment to excess come to a bad end, while the modest who hold to the Way keep their good name. The old saying that we make our own fortune or ruin—here is the evidence.
value.literal: Viewed from this, those who flaunt excess against the times surely end in ill fortune; those who keep the Way and are modest and yielding forever preserve steadfast good fortune. What the ancients called ‘fortune and disaster have no gate—only men summon them’—is this not its proof!

value.zh: 逮于晉難，始自宮掖。
value.en: The Jin dynasty’s catastrophe began in the inner palace.
value.literal: When it came to the Jin calamity, it began in the palace apartments.

value.zh: 楊駿藉武帝之寵私，叨竊非據，賈謐乘惠皇之蒙昧，成此厲階，遂使悼后遇雲林之災，湣懷濫湖城之酷。
value.en: Yang Jun parlayed Emperor Wu’s favor into a post he never deserved; Jia Mi exploited Emperor Hui’s weakness and laid the steps to ruin—so Empress Dao met disaster at Yunlin, and Min Huai suffered cruel abuse at Hucheng.
value.literal: Yang Jun relied on Emperor Wu’s private favor and grasped what he should not have held; Jia Mi rode Emperor Hui’s dullness and made this stair of evil, so that Empress Dao met disaster at Yunlin, and Min Huai suffered cruel abuse at Hucheng.

value.zh: 天人道盡，喪亂弘多，宗廟以之顛覆，黎庶於焉殄瘁。
value.en: Heaven and earth seemed to abandon the house of Jin; chaos spread without end, the altars fell, and the people were ground down.
value.literal: The way of Heaven and men was exhausted; bereavement and chaos were vast; the ancestral temple thereby was overturned; the common people thereby were worn to the bone.

value.zh: 《詩》云：「赫赫宗周，褒姒滅之。」
value.en: The Book of Songs says: ‘Grand stood the house of Zhou—and Baosi brought it down.’
value.literal: The Classic of Poetry says: ‘Splendid was the Zhou of the ancestors—Baosi destroyed it.’

value.zh: 其此之謂也。
value.en: That is exactly what happened here.
value.literal: ’—this is what is meant by that.

value.zh: 爰及江左，未改覆車。
value.en: South of the river they repeated the same fatal mistake.
value.literal: Extending to the left bank of the Yangzi, they did not change the overturned cart.

value.zh: 庾亮世族羽儀，王恭高門領袖，既而職兼出納，任切股肱。
value.en: Yu Liang stood at the head of the great families; Wang Gong led the high-born elite; both held posts that controlled access to the throne and served as the emperor’s right arm.
value.literal: Yu Liang was the plume and standard of great clans; Wang Gong was leader of eminent houses; thereafter their offices combined intake and outgo, and their charge was as close as thigh and arm.

value.zh: 孝伯竟以亡身，元規幾于敗國，豈不哀哉！
value.en: Wang Gong died for it; Yu Liang nearly destroyed the realm—is that not a tragedy?
value.literal: Xiaobo in the end thereby lost his life; Yuankui nearly thereby ruined the state—is it not lamentable!

value.zh: 若褚季野之畏避朝權，王叔仁之固求出鎮，用能全身遠害，有可稱焉。
value.en: Chu Pou shrank from wielding power at court, and Wang Shu begged to be sent to the frontier; both kept their skins and their honor, and deserve mention.
value.literal: As for Chu Yeye’s fearing and avoiding court power, and Wang Shuren’s firmly seeking to go out and hold a command, by this they were able to preserve the body and keep far from harm—there is something to praise in that.

value.zh: 賈充、楊駿、庾亮、王獻之、王恭等已入列傳，其餘既敘其成敗，以為《外戚篇》云。
value.en: Jia Chong, Yang Jun, Yu Liang, Wang Xianzhi, and Wang Gong already have their own chapters; what follows records the rest, gathered here under ‘Imperial Affines.’
value.literal: Jia Chong, Yang Jun, Yu Liang, Wang Xianzhi, Wang Gong, and others have already entered the arrayed biographies; as for the rest, having narrated their success and failure, it is made into this ‘Imperial Affines’ chapter.

value.zh: 羊玄之，惠皇后父，尚書右僕射瑾之子也。
value.en: Yang Xuanzhi, father of Empress Hui, was the son of Yang Jin, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
value.literal: Yang Xuanzhi was the father of Empress Hui and the son of Right Vice Director Jin.

value.zh: 玄之初為尚書郎，以后父，拜光祿大夫、特進、散騎常侍，更封興晉侯。
value.en: He began as a junior secretary in the Department of State Affairs; as the empress’s father he rose to Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, Exalted Marcher, and Regular Cavalier Attendant, and was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Rising Jin.
value.literal: Xuanzhi at first was a Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs; on account of being the empress’s father, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, Exalted Marcher, Regular Cavalier Attendant, and re-enfeoffed as Marquis Who Rouses Jin.

value.zh: 遷尚書右僕射，加侍中，進爵為公。
value.en: He became Right Vice Director, was given the additional post of Palace Attendant, and was raised to ducal rank.
value.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, added as Palace Attendant, and advanced in nobility to duke.

value.zh: 成都王穎之攻長沙王乂也，以討玄之為名，遂憂懼而卒。
value.en: When Sima Ying marched against Sima Yi under the pretext of punishing Yang Xuanzhi, Xuanzhi died of fear and anxiety.
value.literal: When Prince of Chengdu Ying attacked Prince of Changsha Yi, taking punishing Xuanzhi as the name, then in worry and fear he died.

value.zh: 追贈車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。
value.en: He was posthumously honored as General of Chariots and Cavalry with full Three Dukes’ establishment.
value.literal: He was posthumously awarded General of Chariots and Cavalry, opener of office, peer with the Three Dukes.

value.zh: 劉元海（子和） 劉宣
value.en: Liu Yuanhai (with his son He) and Liu Xuan.
value.literal: Liu Yuanhai (son: He) and Liu Xuan.

value.en: (His son He)
value.literal: (Son: He)

value.zh: 劉宣
value.en: Liu Xuan.
value.literal: Liu Xuan.

value.zh: 會豹卒，以元海代為左部帥。
value.en: When Liu Bao died Liu Yuan succeeded him as left-section chief.
value.literal: When Bao died, Yuanhai was appointed in his stead as commander of the left section.

value.zh: 太康末，拜北部都尉。
value.en: Late in Taikang he became northern commandant.
value.literal: At the end of Taikang he was appointed northern commandant.

value.zh: 明刑法，禁奸邪，輕財好施，推誠接物，五部俊傑無不至者。
value.en: He enforced the code, crushed crime, spent freely, dealt honestly, and every notable of the five Xiongnu hosts rallied to him.
value.literal: He clarified penal law, prohibited wickedness, was light with wealth and fond of giving, extended sincerity in receiving people, and there was no outstanding man of the five sections who did not come.

value.zh: 幽冀名儒，後門秀士，不遠千里，亦皆遊焉。
value.en: Confucian stars from You and Ji and poor scholars crossed a thousand li to sit at his feet.
value.literal: Famous Ru of You and Ji, talented men from rear gates, not shying a thousand li, all also came to study with him.

value.zh: 楊駿輔政，以元海為建威將軍、五部大都督，封漢光鄉侯。
value.en: Regent Yang Jun named him General Who Establishes Might, commander-in-chief of the five sections, and marquis of Hanguang township.
value.literal: When Yang Jun assisted the government, he made Yuanhai General Who Establishes Might, grand commander of the five sections, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Han'guang village.

value.zh: 元康末，坐部人叛出塞免官。
value.en: Yuankang's end saw him cashiered when his tribesmen broke for the steppe.
value.literal: At the end of Yuankang he lost office because his tribesmen rebelled and fled beyond the pass.

value.zh: 成都王穎鎮鄴，表元海行甯朔將軍、監五部軍事。
value.en: While Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, was stationed at Ye, he memorialized a request to appoint Yuanhai acting General Who Pacifies the North with supervision over the military affairs of the five divisions.
value.literal: The Prince of Chengdu, Ying, was stationed at Ye and memorialized a request to appoint Yuanhai acting General Who Pacifies the North, with supervision over the military affairs of the five divisions.

value.zh: 惠帝失馭，寇盜蜂起，元海從祖故北部都尉、左賢王劉宣等竊議曰：「昔我先人與漢約為兄弟，憂泰同之。
value.en: As Emperor Hui lost control, Liu Xuan, former northern commandant and left worthy king, whispered with kinsmen: "Our ancestors swore brotherhood with Han and shared its fate.
value.literal: Emperor Hui lost the reins; bandits sprang like wasps; Yuanhai's granduncle, the former northern commandant and Left Worthy King Liu Xuan, and others secretly deliberated, saying, "Formerly our forefathers covenanted with Han as brothers, sharing joy and peril alike.

value.zh: 自漢亡以來，魏晉代興，我單于雖有虛號，無復尺土之業，自諸王侯，降同編戶。
value.en: Since Han fell we have kept a hollow title while every prince sank to commoner status on Jin registers.
value.literal: Since Han fell, Wei and Jin rose in turn; our Shanyu, though he kept an empty title, no longer had an enterprise of a foot of soil; from the various princes and marquises downward he was reduced to the same as registered households.

value.zh: 今司馬氏骨肉相殘，四海鼎沸，興邦復業，此其時矣。
value.en: Now the Simas tear one another apart while the realm boils—this is the moment to refound our line.
value.literal: Now the Sima clan flesh and blood devour one another and the four seas boil; to raise a state and restore an enterprise—this is the time.

value.zh: 左賢王元海姿器絕人，幹宇超世。
value.en: Left Worthy King Liu Yuan's presence and scope outshine every man of his day.
value.literal: Left Worthy King Yuanhai's mien and capacity surpass others, and his stem and canopy transcend the age.

value.zh: 天若不恢崇單于，終不虛生此人也。」
value.en: Heaven would not have bred such a man unless it meant to exalt our Shanyu again."
value.literal: If Heaven does not intend to exalt the Shanyu, in the end it would not vainly have born this man."

value.zh: 於是密共推元海為大單于。
value.en: They secretly elected Liu Yuan great Shanyu.
value.literal: Thereupon they secretly together pushed Yuanhai as great Shanyu.

value.zh: 乃使其党呼延攸詣鄴，以謀告之。
value.en: They sent Huyan You to Ye with the plan.
value.literal: They then sent their partisan Huyan You to Ye to report the plot to him.

value.zh: 元海請歸會葬，穎弗許。
value.en: Liu Yuan begged leave to mourn; Sima Ying refused.
value.literal: Yuanhai requested leave to return for a funeral assembly; Ying did not permit.

value.zh: 乃令攸先歸，告宣等招集五部，引會宜陽諸胡，聲言應穎，實背之也。
value.en: Huyan You raced home to rally the five sections and Yiyang Hu, claiming they would help Sima Ying while plotting the opposite.
value.literal: They then ordered You to return first, telling Xuan and the others to gather the five sections and muster the various Hu at Yiyang, declaring they would answer Ying, but in truth betrayed him.

value.zh: 穎為皇太弟，以元海為太弟屯騎校尉。
value.en: When Sima Ying became crown younger brother, Liu Yuan became his garrison-cavalry colonel.
value.literal: When Ying became imperial younger brother, he made Yuanhai Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry of the imperial younger brother.

value.zh: 惠帝伐穎，次於蕩陰，穎假元海輔國將軍、督北城守事。
value.en: During Emperor Hui's march on Dangyin, Sima Ying put Liu Yuan in charge of the northern wall.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui attacked Ying and halted at Dangyin, Ying made Yuanhai acting General Who Supports the State and supervised defence of the north wall.

value.zh: 及六軍敗績，穎以元海為冠軍將軍，封盧奴伯。
value.en: After the six armies collapsed Sima Ying named him General Who Crowns the Army and baron of Lunu.
value.literal: When the six armies were routed, Ying made Yuanhai General Who Crowns the Army and enfeoffed him as Baron of Lunu.

value.zh: 并州刺史東嬴公騰、安北將軍王浚，起兵伐穎，元海說穎曰：「今二鎮跋扈，眾餘十萬，恐非宿衛及近都士庶所能禦之，請為殿下還說五部，以赴國難。」
value.en: When Bingzhou governor Sima Teng and Wang Jun raised troops against Sima Ying with more than a hundred thousand men, Liu Yuan advised Ying: "The two commands are now overbearing, and I fear neither the palace guard nor the people near the capital can withstand them. Let me return for Your Highness and persuade the five Xiongnu divisions to answer the state's crisis."
value.literal: Governor of Bing Sima Teng of Dongying and General Who Guards the North Wang Jun raised troops to attack Ying; Yuanhai counselled Ying, saying, "Now the two garrisons are overbearing; their hosts exceed a hundred thousand—I fear neither the palace guard nor the gentry near the capital can withstand them; I beg leave for Your Highness to return and persuade the five sections to answer the state's disaster."

value.zh: 穎曰：「五部之眾可保發已不？
value.en: Sima Ying asked, "Can you actually raise those five hosts?
value.literal: Ying said, "Can the host of the five sections be guaranteed to mobilize?

value.zh: 縱能發之，鮮卑、烏丸勁速如風雲，何易可當邪？
value.en: Even if you can, Xianbei and Wuhuan move like storms—who stops them once loosed?
value.literal: Even if they can be mobilized, Xianbei and Wuhuan are fierce and swift as wind and cloud—how can they easily be resisted?

value.zh: 吾欲奉乘輿還洛陽，避其鋒銳，徐傳檄天下，以逆順制之。
value.en: I mean to escort the throne to Luoyang, dodge their spearpoint, then call the realm to arms on right and wrong.
value.literal: I wish to escort the imperial carriage back to Luoyang, avoid their sharp edge, then slowly transmit summons across All-under-Heaven and control them with obedience and rebellion.

value.zh: 君意何如？」
value.en: What do you counsel?"
value.literal: What is your intent?"

value.zh: 元海曰：「殿下武皇帝之子，有殊勳於王室，威恩光洽，四海欽風，孰不思為殿下沒命投軀者哉，何難發之有乎！
value.en: Liu Yuan answered, "You are Sima Yan's son, beloved across the realm—every warrior would die for you; raising the tribes is no hard task.
value.literal: Yuanhai said, "Your Highness is Martial Emperor's son and has extraordinary merit toward the royal house; awe and kindness shine everywhere, and the four seas admire your wind—who would not think to die and cast aside his body for Your Highness—what difficulty is there in mobilizing them!

value.zh: 王浚豎子，東嬴疏屬，豈能與殿下爭衡邪！
value.en: Wang Jun is a pup and Sima Teng a cadet branch—neither can rival you.
value.literal: Wang Jun is a stripling; Dongying is a distant cousin—how can they match Your Highness!

value.zh: 殿下一發鄴宮，示弱於人，洛陽可復至乎？
value.en: Flee Ye once and you advertise weakness—will Luoyang ever welcome you back?
value.literal: If Your Highness once leaves the Ye palace, you show weakness to men—can Luoyang be regained?

value.zh: 縱達洛陽，威權不復在殿下也。
value.en: Even in Luoyang you would hold no real power.
value.literal: Even if you reach Luoyang, awesome authority will no longer be with Your Highness.

value.zh: 紙檄尺書，誰為人奉之！
value.en: Who would heed a sheaf of edicts from a discrowned prince!
value.literal: Paper summons an inch long—who will obey them!

value.zh: 且東胡之悍不逾五部，願殿下勉撫士眾，靖以鎮之，當為殿下以二部摧東嬴，三部梟王浚，二豎之首可指日而懸矣。」
value.en: The eastern tribes are no tougher than our horsemen—stay in Ye, steady the army, and I will smash Sima Teng with two wings and take Wang Jun's head with three; both puppets will swing from the gate in days."
value.literal: Moreover the eastern Hu are not fiercer than the five sections; I hope Your Highness will encourage and soothe the soldiers and quiet them to hold the city—I will for Your Highness with two sections crush Dongying and with three sections behead Wang Jun; the two striplings' heads can be hung within days."

value.zh: 穎悅，拜元海為北單于、參丞相軍事。
value.en: Sima Ying cheered up, named Liu Yuan northern Shanyu, and attached him to the chancellor's staff.
value.literal: Ying was pleased, appointed Yuanhai northern Shanyu, and joined him to the staff of the minister of state.

value.zh: 元海至左國城，劉宣等上大單于之號，二旬之間，眾已五萬，都于離石。
value.en: At Zuoguocheng Liu Xuan proclaimed him great Shanyu; inside twenty days fifty thousand men gathered with capital at Lishi.
value.literal: Yuanhai reached Zuoguocheng; Liu Xuan and others presented the title of great Shanyu; within twenty days the host already numbered fifty thousand, with capital at Lishi.

value.zh: 王浚使將軍祁弘率鮮卑攻鄴，穎敗，挾天子南奔洛陽。
value.en: Wang Jun's general Qi Hong drove Xianbei against Ye; Sima Ying fled south clutching the emperor.
value.literal: Wang Jun sent General Qi Hong leading Xianbei to attack Ye; Ying was defeated, seized the Son of Heaven, and fled south to Luoyang.

value.zh: 元海曰：「穎不用吾言，逆自奔潰，真奴才也。
value.en: Liu Yuan sneered, "Sima Ying ignored my counsel and ran—little better than a bondsman.
value.literal: Yuanhai said, "Ying did not use my words and contrary-wise fled in collapse—he is a true slave.

value.zh: 然吾與其有言矣，不可不救。」
value.en: Still I promised him aid and must move."
value.literal: Yet I had an agreement with him and cannot fail to save him."

value.zh: 於是命右於陸王劉景、左獨鹿王劉延年等率步騎二萬，將討鮮卑。
value.en: He ordered Liu Jing and Liu Yannian forward with twenty thousand riders—ostensibly against the Xianbei.
value.literal: Thereupon he ordered King of the Right Yulu Liu Jing, King of the Left Duliu Liu Yannian, and others to lead twenty thousand foot and horse, about to attack the Xianbei.

value.zh: 劉宣等固諫曰：「晉為無道，奴隸禦我，是以右賢王猛不勝其忿。
value.en: Liu Xuan blocked him: "Jin treats us like driven slaves—remember how Right Worthy Meng rose in fury.
value.literal: Liu Xuan and others firmly remonstrated, saying, "Jin is without the Way; slaves drive us—therefore the Right Worthy King Meng could not bear his rage.

value.zh: 屬晉綱未馳，大事不遂，右賢塗地，單于之恥也。
value.en: Jin's grip was still tight then, and our rising failed—our people's blood is still the Shanyu's shame.
value.literal: When Jin's net had not yet slackened, the great matter did not succeed; the Right Worthy was crushed to earth—it was the Shanyu's shame.

value.zh: 今司馬氏父子兄弟自相魚肉，此天厭晉德，授之於我。
value.en: Now the Simas devour their own—Heaven has turned from Jin and hands us the mandate.
value.literal: Now the Sima father, sons, and brothers devour one another like fish flesh—Heaven tires of Jin's virtue and hands it to us.

value.zh: 單于積德在躬，為晉人所服，方當興我邦族，復呼韓邪之業，鮮卑、烏丸可以為援，奈何距之而拯仇敵！
value.en: You already command Jin's awe; rebuild our nation and Huhanye's glory—use the steppe peoples, do not waste your strength saving a foe.
value.literal: The Shanyu has stored virtue in his person and is obeyed by Jin men; you should raise our tribal nation, restore Huhanye's enterprise—Xianbei and Wuhuan can be allies—how turn them away to rescue an enemy!

value.zh: 今天假手於我，不可違也。
value.en: Heaven lends us this chance—we dare not refuse.
value.literal: Now Heaven lends its hand to us—it cannot be disobeyed.

value.zh: 違天不祥，逆眾不濟；
value.en: Defy Heaven and fortune flees; defy your warriors and nothing succeeds;
value.literal: To disobey Heaven is inauspicious; to oppose the multitude will not succeed;

value.zh: 天與不取，反受其咎。
value.en: Reject Heaven's gift and you earn its curse.
value.literal: Heaven gives and you do not take—instead you receive its blame.

value.zh: 願單于勿疑。」
value.en: Do not hesitate, Shanyu."
value.literal: I beg the Shanyu not to doubt."

value.zh: 元海曰：「善。
value.en: Liu Yuan said, "Well spoken.
value.literal: Yuanhai said, "Good.

value.zh: 當為崇岡峻阜，何能為培塿乎！
value.en: We aim to be mountain ranges, not molehills.
value.literal: We ought to be high ridges and steep mounds—how can we be mere hillocks!

value.zh: 夫帝王豈有常哉，大禹出於西戎，文王生於東夷，顧惟德所授耳。
value.en: Thrones never stay fixed: Yu rose from western tribes, Wen from eastern barbarians—virtue alone decides who rules.
value.literal: For emperors and kings—how can there be constancy? Great Yu came from the western Rong; King Wen was born among the eastern Yi—it depends only on whom virtue invests.

value.zh: 今見眾十餘萬，皆一當晉十，鼓行而摧亂晉，猶拉枯耳。
value.en: I command a hundred thousand, each man worth ten Jin soldiers; marching on Luoyang will splinter them like dry twigs.
value.literal: Now I see a host of over a hundred thousand, each one worth ten Jin soldiers; beating the drum and advancing to crush chaotic Jin is like snapping dead wood.

value.zh: 上可成漢高之業，下不失為魏氏。
value.en: Best case I match Han Gaozu; worst I still rival Cao Wei.
value.literal: Above I can complete Gaozu's enterprise; below I will not fall short of the house of Wei.

value.zh: 雖然，晉人未必同我。
value.en: Yet Jin subjects may not flock to us.
value.literal: Even so, Jin men will not necessarily join me.

value.zh: 漢有天下世長，恩德結于人心，是以昭烈崎嶇於一州之地，而能抗衡於天下。
value.en: Han ruled long enough that the people still love its memory—Liu Bei clung to one province yet defied the world.
value.literal: Han possessed the realm for generations long; kindness and virtue knotted in human hearts; therefore Zhaolie, twisted on one province's ground, could yet resist All-under-Heaven.

value.zh: 吾又漢氏之甥，約為兄弟，兄亡弟紹，不亦可乎？
value.en: We are sworn brothers to the Liu house; when the elder line fell should not the younger inherit?
value.literal: I am moreover Han's nephew by marriage, covenanted as brothers; the elder died and the younger continues—is that not fitting?

value.zh: 且可稱漢，追尊後主，以懷人望。」
value.en: Call our state Han, enshrine the last Han emperor, and the hearts of the people will follow."
value.literal: Moreover one may style the state Han, posthumously honour the last lord, and thereby embrace human hope."

value.zh: 乃遷于左國城，遠人歸附者數萬。
value.en: He shifted to Zuoguocheng and tens of thousands of far wanderers joined him.
value.literal: Thereupon he moved to Zuoguocheng, and distant people who attached numbered in the tens of thousands.

value.zh: 南齊書卷第五 本紀第五
value.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 5, Annals 5
value.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 5, Annals 5

value.zh: 史臣曰：郭璞稱永昌之名，有二日之象，而隆昌之號亦同焉。
value.en: The historian says: Guo Pu held that the name Yongchang bears the sign of two suns—and the era name Longchang is likewise.
value.literal: The historian says: Guo Pu said the name Yongchang has the image of two suns—and the era name Longchang is the same.

value.zh: 案漢中平六年，獻帝卽位，便改元爲光熹，張讓、段珪誅後，改元爲昭寧，董卓輔政，改元爲永漢，一歲四號也。
value.en: It is on record that in Han Zhongping 6, when Emperor Xian ascended, the era was at once changed to Guangxi; after Zhang Rang and Duan Gui were killed it became Zhaoning; when Dong Zhuo seized power it became Yonghan—four era names in one year.
value.literal: It is recorded that in Han Zhongping 6, when Emperor Xian took the throne he at once changed the era to Guangxi; after the execution of Zhang Rang and Duan Gui it was changed to Zhaoning; when Dong Zhuo held the government it was changed to Yonghan—four era names in one year.

value.zh: 晉惠帝太安二年，長沙王乂事敗，成都王穎改元爲永安；
value.en: In Jin, Emperor Hui's Taian 2, when Prince Yi of Changsha fell, Prince Ying of Chengdu changed the era to Yongan;
value.literal: In Jin Emperor Hui's Taian 2, when Prince Yi of Changsha's affair failed, Prince Ying of Chengdu changed the era to Yongan;

value.zh: 穎自鄴奪，河間王顒復改元爲永興，一歲三號也。
value.en: when Ying seized rule from Ye, Prince Yong of Hejian changed the era again to Yongxing—three era names in one year.
value.literal: when Ying seized power from Ye, Prince Yong of Hejian again changed the era to Yongxing—three era names in one year.

value.zh: 隆昌、延興、建武，亦三改年號。
value.en: Longchang, Yanxing, and Jianwu likewise saw three changes of era name.
value.literal: Longchang, Yanxing, and Jianwu also saw three era changes.

value.zh: 故知喪亂之軌迹，雖千載而必同矣。
value.en: Thus one knows that the path of chaos and collapse, though a thousand years lie between, is always the same.
value.literal: Thus one knows that the track of turmoil and ruin, though a thousand years apart, is sure to be the same.

value.zh: 列傳第五十九
value.en: the 59th year of Biography
value.literal: Biographies number fifty-nine

value.zh: 自天厭梁德，多難薦臻，寰宇分崩，英雄互起，不可勝紀，人人自以為得之。
value.en: Since Heaven grew weary of the Liang and hardships followed one upon another, the realm split apart and heroes rose beyond counting, each believing he held destiny in his hand.
value.literal: Since Heaven grew weary of Liang's virtue and many hardships came in succession, the realm split apart and heroes rose against one another beyond counting; each man thought he had grasped success.

value.zh: 然夷凶翦亂，拯溺扶危，四海樂推，三靈眷命，揖讓而居南面者，陳氏也。
value.en: Yet it was the house of Chen that quelled the wicked, rescued the drowning, and upheld the endangered; that the four seas joyfully advanced, that the three numina favored, and that through abdication took the throne.
value.literal: Yet it was the Chen who quelled the barbarous and cut down disorder, rescued the drowning and upheld the endangered, were joyfully advanced by the four seas, were favored by the three numina, and through yielding ceremony took the facing-south position.

value.zh: 豈非歷數有在，惟天所授，當璧應運，其事甚明，一也。
value.en: Is this not because the mandate of fate was fixed and Heaven alone bestowed it, the jade disk answering the age? This is clear—the first point.
value.literal: Is this not because the cycle of fate had its place and Heaven alone bestowed it—the jade disk answering the age? This matter is very clear—the first point.

value.zh: 主上承基，明德遠被，天綱再張，地維重紐。
value.en: Our sovereign has inherited the foundation. His bright virtue spreads far. Heaven's net is stretched anew and Earth's cords are bound again.
value.literal: The sovereign inherits the foundation; bright virtue spreads far; Heaven's net is stretched anew; Earth's cords are bound again.

value.zh: 夫以王琳之強，侯瑱之力，進足以搖盪中原，爭衡天下，退足以屈強江外，雄張偏隅。
value.en: Consider Wang Lin's strength and Hou Tian's power. Advancing, they could shake the central plains and contend for the realm. Retreating, they could hold the Yangzi south and dominate a corner.
value.literal: Consider Wang Lin's strength and Hou Tian's power: advancing, they were enough to shake the central plains and contend for the realm; retreating, enough to bend the strong beyond the Yangzi and dominate a corner.

value.zh: 然或命一旅之師，或資一士之說，琳即瓦解冰泮，投身異域，瑱則厥角稽顙，委命闕庭。
value.en: Yet with a single brigade sent, or with one man's counsel relied upon, Lin dissolved like melting ice and fled to foreign lands, while Tian bowed his forehead to the ground and surrendered at the imperial court.
value.literal: Yet with only a single brigade sent, or relying on one man's persuasion, Lin at once dissolved like ice melting, casting himself into foreign lands; Tian bowed forehead to ground and entrusted his fate to the imperial court.

value.zh: 斯又天假之威，而除其患，其事甚明，二也。
value.en: This again is Heaven lending its might to remove such threats. This is clear—the second point.
value.literal: This again is Heaven lending its might to remove their peril—this matter is very clear—the second point.
