value.zh: 今將軍以藩戚之重，擁東南之眾，盡忠奉上，戮力勤王，豈不勳高竇融，寵過吳芮，析珪判野，南面稱孤，其事甚明，三也。
value.en: You bear the weight of an imperial kinsman on the frontier and command the hosts of the southeast. If you devote your loyalty to the throne and join your strength to the royal cause, would your merit not exceed Dou Rong's and your favor surpass Wu Rui's, with jade tallies divided and lands apportioned, reigning in your domain? This is clear—the third point.
value.literal: Now the General, with the weight of a frontier kinsman, holds the hosts of the southeast; if you exhaust loyalty in serving above and join strength to aid the throne, would your merit not exceed Dou Rong's, your favor surpass Wu Rui's, with jade tallies divided and fields apportioned, facing south and styled solitary lord? This matter is very clear—the third point.

value.zh: 且聖朝棄瑕忘過，寬厚待人，改過自新，咸加敘擢。
value.en: Moreover the court discards flaws and forgets faults, treats men with generous breadth, and promotes all who reform and renew themselves.
value.literal: Moreover the holy court discards flaws and forgets faults, treats men with generous breadth, and those who reform and renew themselves are all promoted in rank.

value.zh: 至如余孝頃、潘純陀、李孝欽、歐陽頠等，悉委以心腹，任以爪牙，胸中豁然，曾無纖芥。
value.en: Men such as Yu Xiaoxiang, Pan Chuntuo, Li Xiaoqin, and Ouyang Hui were all entrusted as inner confidants and employed as his claws and fangs. The sovereign's heart remained open, without the slightest grudge.
value.literal: As for Yu Xiaoxiang, Pan Chuntuo, Li Xiaoqin, Ouyang Hui, and the like—all were entrusted as inner confidants and employed as claws and fangs; the breast was open and clear, never a fiber of resentment.

value.zh: 況將軍釁非張繡，罪異畢諶，當何慮于危亡，何失于富貴？
value.en: Your offense is not Zhang Xiu's, your crime differs from Bi Chen's. Why should you fear ruin or lose wealth and honor?
value.literal: How much more so for the General, whose offense is not Zhang Xiu's, whose crime differs from Bi Chen's—why should you fear ruin, why lose wealth and honor?

value.zh: 此又其事甚明，四也。
value.en: This too is clear—the fourth point.
value.literal: This again is very clear—the fourth point.

value.zh: 方今周、齊鄰睦，境外無虞，並兵一向，匪朝伊夕。
value.en: At present Northern Zhou and Qi are friendly neighbors. Beyond the borders there is no worry, yet their united armies may strike at any moment—not merely tomorrow or the day after.
value.literal: At present Zhou and Qi are neighbors in harmony; beyond the borders there is no worry; united armies will strike in one direction—not merely tomorrow or the day after.

value.zh: 非有劉、項競逐之機，楚、趙連從之事，可得雍容高拱，坐論西伯，其事甚明，五也。
value.en: There is no occasion like Liu Bang and Xiang Yu contending for the realm, no alliance like Chu and Zhao joining forces. You cannot at ease with folded hands sit and discourse like the Earl of the West. This is clear—the fifth point.
value.literal: There is no occasion like Liu and Xiang contending, no matter like Chu and Zhao joining in alliance—you cannot at ease with hands folded sit and discourse like the Earl of the West. This is very clear—the fifth point.

value.zh: 且留將軍狼顧一隅，亟經摧衄，聲實虧喪，膽氣衰沮。
value.en: Moreover General Liu, holding one corner like a wolf glancing backward, has suffered defeat after defeat. His reputation is ruined and his courage broken.
value.literal: Moreover General Liu, wolf-glancing in one corner, has repeatedly suffered defeats; reputation and substance are diminished, courage and spirit decayed.

value.zh: 高瓖、向文政、留瑜、黃子玉此數人者，將軍所知，首鼠兩端，唯利是視，其餘將帥亦可見矣。
value.en: Gao Rang, Xiang Wenzheng, Liu Yu, and Huang Ziyu—these men you know well—are fence-sitters who look only to profit. The rest of your commanders are no better.
value.literal: Gao Rang, Xiang Wenzheng, Liu Yu, Huang Ziyu—these several men, as the General knows, are rats with two heads, looking only to profit; the rest of the commanders may likewise be seen.

value.zh: 孰能被堅執銳，長驅深入，系馬埋輪，奮不顧命，以先士卒者乎？
value.en: Who among them can don hard armor, grasp sharp blades, drive deep into enemy territory, tether horses and bury wheels, and charge ahead of the ranks without regard for his life?
value.literal: Who among them can don hard armor and grasp sharp blades, drive far in deep penetration, tether horses and bury wheels, strive without regard for life, and lead before the soldiers?

value.zh: 此又其事甚明，六也。
value.en: This too is clear—the sixth point.
value.literal: This again is very clear—the sixth point.

value.zh: 且將軍之強，孰如侯景？
value.en: Moreover, is your strength equal to Hou Jing's?
value.literal: Moreover, is the General's strength equal to Hou Jing's?

value.zh: 將軍之眾，孰如王琳？
value.en: Are your troops equal to Wang Lin's?
value.literal: Are the General's hosts equal to Wang Lin's?

value.zh: 武皇滅侯景於前，今上摧王琳於後，此乃天時，非復人力。
value.en: The Martial Emperor destroyed Hou Jing before; our present sovereign crushed Wang Lin after. This is Heaven's season, not human strength alone.
value.literal: The Martial Emperor destroyed Hou Jing before; the present sovereign crushed Wang Lin after—this is Heaven's season, no longer human effort.

value.zh: 且兵革已後，人皆厭亂，其孰能棄墳墓，捐妻子，出萬死不顧之計，從將軍于白刃之間乎？
value.en: After years of war, all men are weary of disorder. Who would abandon his ancestors' graves, cast off wife and children, and follow you between flashing blades in a plan that courts ten thousand deaths?
value.literal: Moreover, after arms and armor, all men are weary of disorder—who could abandon graves, cast off wife and children, adopt a plan of ten thousand deaths without regard, and follow the General between flashing blades?

value.zh: 此又其事甚明，七也。
value.en: This too is clear—the seventh point.
value.literal: This again is very clear—the seventh point.

value.zh: 曆觀前古，鑒之往事，子陽、季孟傾覆相尋，餘善、右渠危亡繼及，天命可畏，山川難恃。
value.en: Surveying former ages and taking past events as mirror, Ziyang and Jimeng fell in succession, Yushan and Youqu perished one after another. Heaven's mandate is to be feared; mountains and rivers are hard to rely on.
value.literal: Reviewing former ages and taking past events as mirror, Ziyang and Jimeng fell in succession, Yushan and Youqu perished one after another—Heaven's mandate is to be feared, mountains and rivers are hard to rely on.

value.zh: 況將軍欲以數郡之地，當天下之兵，以諸侯之資，拒天子之命，強弱逆順，可得侔乎？
value.en: How much less can you, with the lands of a few commanderies, meet the armies of the realm, or with a feudal lord's resources refuse the Son of Heaven's command? Can strength and weakness, obedience and rebellion, be matched?
value.literal: How much more if the General wishes with the lands of a few commanderies to meet the armies of the realm, with a feudal lord's resources to refuse the Son of Heaven's command—can strength and weakness, obedience and rebellion, be matched?

value.zh: 此又其事甚明，八也。
value.en: This too is clear—the eighth point.
value.literal: This again is very clear—the eighth point.

value.zh: 且非我族類，其心必異，不愛其親，豈能及物？
value.en: Moreover, those not of our kindred must differ in heart. If one does not love his kin, how can he care for others?
value.literal: Moreover, those not of our kindred—their hearts must differ; if one does not love his kin, how can he reach to other things?

value.zh: 留將軍身縻國爵，子尚王姬，猶且棄天屬而弗顧，背明君而孤立，危急之日，豈能同憂共患，不背將軍者乎？
value.en: General Liu holds state rank and his son is married to an imperial princess, yet he still abandons his kin and turns his back on the enlightened sovereign to stand alone. In days of peril, how could he share your worry and not turn against you?
value.literal: General Liu is bound by state rank, his son married to an imperial princess—yet he still abandons Heaven's kin without regard and turns his back on the enlightened lord to stand alone; in days of peril, how could he share worry and disaster and not turn against the General?

value.zh: 至於師老力屈，懼誅利賞，必有韓、智晉陽之謀，張、陳井陘之事。
value.en: When troops grow weary and strength fails, when men fear punishment and covet reward, there will surely be plots like those of Han and Zhi at Jinyang and affairs like those of Zhang and Chen at Jingxing Pass.
value.literal: As for troops worn and strength spent, fearing punishment and coveting reward—there will surely be plots like Han and Zhi at Jinyang, affairs like Zhang and Chen at Jingxing Pass.

value.zh: 此又其事甚明，九也。
value.en: This too is clear—the ninth point.
value.literal: This again is very clear—the ninth point.

value.zh: 且北軍萬里遠鬥，鋒不可當，將軍自戰其地，人多顧後，梁安背向為心，修忤匹夫之力，眾寡不敵，將帥不侔，師以無名而出，事以無機而動，以此稱兵，未知其利。
value.en: The northern army fights from ten thousand li away, yet its edge cannot be withstood. You fight on your own ground, yet your men look behind them. Liang An's heart has turned away. Xiu can defy only a common man's strength. Many and few do not match; commanders are unequal. Your army goes forth without righteous cause and moves without opportune moment. To raise arms on this basis—I do not see the profit.
value.literal: Moreover the northern army fights from ten thousand li away yet its edge cannot be withstood; the General fights on your own ground—men mostly look behind; Liang An's heart turns away; Xiu defies a common man's strength; many and few do not match, commanders are not equal; the army goes forth without righteous name, the affair moves without opportune moment—by this to raise arms, one does not know the profit.

value.zh: 夫以漢朝吳、楚，晉室穎、顒，連城數十，長戟百萬，拔本塞源，自圖家國，其有成功者乎？
value.en: Consider Han's Wu and Chu, Jin's Ying and Yong—linked cities by the tens, long halberds by the million, uprooting the root and blocking the source to plot for themselves—were there any who succeeded?
value.literal: Consider Han's Wu and Chu, Jin's Ying and Yong—linked cities by the tens, long halberds by the million, uprooting the root and blocking the source, plotting state and clan for themselves—were there any who succeeded?

value.zh: 此又其事甚明，十也。
value.en: This too is clear—the tenth point.
value.literal: This again is very clear—the tenth point.

value.zh: 孫靜字幼臺，堅季弟也。
value.en: Sun Jing, styled Youtai, was the youngest of Sun Jian’s brothers.
value.literal: Sun Jing, courtesy name Youtai, was the youngest younger brother of Sun Jian.

value.zh: 堅始舉事，靜糾合鄉曲及宗室五六百人以為保障，眾咸附焉。
value.en: When Sun Jian first rose in arms, Sun Jing rallied some five or six hundred local men and kinsmen as a protective force, and people flocked to him.
value.literal: When Sun Jian first raised troops, Jing gathered five or six hundred men from the villages and the clan to serve as a safeguard, and the masses all attached themselves to him.

value.zh: 策破劉繇，定諸縣。
value.en: Sun Ce defeated Liu Yao and brought the counties under control.
value.literal: Ce defeated Liu Yao and pacified the various counties.

value.zh: 進攻會稽，遣人請靜，靜將家屬與策會於錢唐。
value.en: He pressed the attack on Kuaiji, sent for Sun Jing, and Sun Jing brought his household to join Sun Ce at Qiantang.
value.literal: Advancing to attack Kuaiji, he sent someone to summon Jing; Jing led his family members and met Ce at Qiantang.

value.zh: 是時太守王朗拒策於固陵，策數渡水戰，不能克。
value.en: The prefect Wang Lang held Sun Ce off at Guling; Sun Ce tried more than once to force a crossing and fight on the other bank but could not break through.
value.literal: At that time the Administrator Wang Lang resisted Ce at Guling; Ce several times crossed the water to give battle but could not overcome him.

value.zh: 靜說策曰："朗負阻城守，難可卒拔。
value.en: Sun Jing urged Sun Ce: Wang Lang is dug in behind natural barriers; you cannot expect to storm him overnight.
value.literal: Jing urged Ce, saying, Lang relies on natural obstacles and defends the city; he is hard to take in a hurry.

value.zh: 查瀆南去此數十里，
value.en: Zha Creek lies a few dozen li to the south,
value.literal: Zha Creek is several tens of li south of here,

value.zh: 〈查音祖加反。〉
value.en: 〈The marginal gloss indicates that Zha takes its initial from zu and its rime from jia.〉
value.literal: 〈Note on pronunciation: the character for Zha is read zu-jia [fanqie].〉

value.zh: 而道之要徑也，宜從彼據其內，所謂攻其無備、出其不意者也。
value.en: That route is the vital approach; thrust inland along it and strike where they do not expect you.
value.literal: and it is a crucial path; you ought to advance by that route and seize what lies within—what is called striking where they are unprepared and catching them unawares.

value.zh: 吾當自帥眾為軍前隊，破之必矣。
value.en: I will lead the main body myself as the first wave—we will crack them for certain.
value.literal: I shall personally lead the host as the vanguard of the army; we will surely break them.

value.zh: "策曰："善。
value.en: Sun Ce replied, Good.
value.literal: Ce said, Good.

value.zh: "乃詐令軍中曰："頃連雨水濁，兵飲之多腹痛，令促具罌缶數百口澄水。
value.en: Then he put out a false order: The river has been silty from all this rain; men who drink it are doubled up with cramps—have them ready hundreds of jars at once to draw off clear water.
value.literal: Then he falsely announced to the army: The rains have lately turned the water muddy; the soldiers drinking it have mostly gotten stomachaches—order them quickly to prepare several hundred jars and pots to settle the water.

value.zh: "至昏暮，羅以然火誑朗，便分軍夜投查瀆道，襲高遷屯。
value.en: At nightfall he lit decoy fires to fool Wang Lang, split his force, and marched up the Zha Creek track after dark to strike the camp at Gaoxian.
value.literal: At dusk he spread fires to deceive Lang, then divided the army and by night sent them along the Zha Creek road to raid the Gaoxian camp.

value.zh: 〈臣松之案：今永兴县有高迁桥。〉
value.en: 〈Pei Songzhi notes that Gaoxian Bridge still stands in present-day Yongxing County.〉
value.literal: 〈Pei Songzhi’s investigation: today in Yongxing County there is a Gaoxian Bridge.〉

value.zh: 朗大驚。
value.en: Wang Lang was thrown into panic.
value.literal: Lang was greatly alarmed.

value.zh: 遣故丹楊太守周昕等帥兵前戰。
value.en: He dispatched the former Danyang prefect Zhou Xin and others to take the lead with their men.
value.literal: He sent the former Danyang Administrator Zhou Xin and others to lead troops forward into battle.

value.zh: 策破昕等，斬之，遂定會稽。
value.en: Sun Ce routed them, killed Zhou Xin, and settled Kuaiji.
value.literal: Ce defeated Xin and the others, beheaded them, and thereupon pacified Kuaiji.

value.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：昕字大明。
value.en: 〈According to the Kuaiji dianlu, Zhou Xin’s courtesy name was Daming.
value.literal: 〈The Kuaiji Canon Record states: Xin’s courtesy name was Daming.

value.zh: 少游京师，师事太傅陈蕃，博览群书，明於风角，善推灾异。
value.en: He had studied in the capital under Grand Tutor Chen Fan, read widely, and was adept at astrological signs and reading portents.
value.literal: In his youth he traveled to the capital and studied under Grand Tutor Chen Fan; he read widely and was skilled in “wind-angle” divination and interpreting anomalies.

value.zh: 辟太尉府，举高第，稍迁丹杨太守。
value.en: He entered the Grand Commandant’s service, graduated with highest honors, and rose step by step to prefect of Danyang.
value.literal: He was summoned to the Grand Commandant’s office, ranked at the top of his cohort, and was gradually promoted to Danyang Administrator.

value.zh: 曹公起义兵，昕前后遣兵万餘人助公征伐。
value.en: When Cao Cao raised his coalition army, Zhou Xin repeatedly sent him upward of ten thousand men for the campaigns.
value.literal: When Duke Cao raised the righteous army, Xin in succession sent more than ten thousand troops to assist the duke in his expeditions.

value.zh: 袁术之在淮南也，昕恶其淫虐，绝不与通。
value.en: While Yuan Shu occupied Huainan, Zhou Xin abhorred his cruelty and dissipation and would have nothing to do with him.
value.literal: When Yuan Shu was in Huainan, Xin detested his debauchery and cruelty and utterly refused dealings with him.

value.zh: 献帝春秋曰：袁术遣吴景攻昕，未拔，景乃募百姓敢从周昕者死不赦。
value.en: The Xiandi Chunqiu records that Yuan Shu sent Wu Jing against Zhou Xin without reducing him; Wu Jing then threatened the populace that anyone who sided with Zhou Xin would die without mercy.
value.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian states: Yuan Shu sent Wu Jing to attack Xin but did not capture him; Jing then promised the common people that whoever dared follow Zhou Xin would be put to death without pardon.

value.zh: 昕曰：“我则不德，百姓何罪？”
value.en: Zhou Xin said, If I am the one at fault, what have the people done wrong?
value.literal: Xin said, If I lack virtue, what crime have the common people committed?

value.zh: 遂散兵，还本郡。〉
value.en: So he sent his soldiers home and withdrew to his own commandery.
value.literal: Thereupon he dispersed his troops and returned to his native commandery.

value.zh: 表拜靜為奮武校尉，欲授之重任，靜戀墳墓宗族，不樂出仕，求留鎮守。
value.en: Sun Ce recommended him as Colonel Who Inspires Martial Might and meant to give him a major post, but Sun Jing was unwilling to leave his family graves and kin and asked instead to stay and hold the territory.
value.literal: [Sun Ce] memorialized and appointed Jing Colonel Who Inspires Martial Might, wishing to give him heavy responsibility; Jing was attached to his ancestral graves and clan and did not relish leaving office, and asked to remain to guard and hold the region.

value.zh: 策從之。
value.en: Sun Ce agreed.
value.literal: Ce granted his request.

value.zh: 權統事，就遷昭義中郎將，終於家。
value.en: When Sun Quan took charge, Sun Jing was promoted in place to General of the Household Gentlemen of Manifest Righteousness and ended his days at home.
value.literal: When Quan assumed direction of affairs, [Jing] was promoted on the spot to General of the Household Gentlemen of Manifest Righteousness and died at home.

value.zh: 有五子，皓、瑜、皎、奐、謙。
value.en: He had five sons—Hao, Yu, Jiao, Huan, and Qian.
value.literal: He had five sons: Hao, Yu, Jiao, Huan, and Qian.

value.zh: 皓三子：綽、超、恭。
value.en: Sun Hao had three sons: Chuo, Chao, and Gong.
value.literal: Hao had three sons: Chuo, Chao, and Gong.

value.zh: 超為偏將軍。
value.en: Sun Chao rose to General of the Left.
value.literal: Chao served as General of the Left.

value.zh: 恭生峻。
value.en: Sun Gong was the father of Sun Jun.
value.literal: Gong fathered Jun.

value.zh: 綽生綝。
value.en: Sun Chuo was the father of Sun Lin.
value.literal: Chuo fathered Lin.

value.zh: 鄰年九歲，代領豫章，近封都鄉侯。
value.en: Sun Lin took Yuzhang at nine and soon received the marquisate of Dou township.
value.literal: At age nine Lin replaced him as leader of Yuzhang and was shortly enfeoffed Marquis of Dou Township.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：邻字公达，雅性精敏，幼有令誉。〉
value.en: 〈The Wu shu: Sun Lin, styled Gongda, was acute and polished and famed even as a boy.〉
value.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: Lin’s courtesy name was Gongda; by nature he was refined, keen, and from youth had a fine reputation.〉

value.zh: 在郡垂二十年，討平叛賊，功績修理。
value.en: For almost twenty years in the prefecture he crushed rebels and ran an orderly administration.
value.literal: In the commandery nearly twenty years, he suppressed and pacified rebel bandits; his achievements and administration were orderly.

value.zh: 召還武昌，為繞帳督。
value.en: Recalled to Wuchang, he commanded the headquarters guard.
value.literal: He was summoned back to Wuchang and became commander of the tent guard.

value.zh: 時太常潘浚掌荊州事，重安長陳留舒燮有罪下獄，浚嘗失燮，欲置之於法。
value.en: Minister Pan Jun then governed Jingzhou; Shu Xie of Chenliu, magistrate of Chong’an, stood accused—Pan Jun had old grievances and meant to punish him.
value.literal: At that time Minister of Ceremonies Pan Jun oversaw Jing Province affairs; the magistrate of Chong’an, Shu Xie of Chenliu, was guilty and imprisoned; Jun had once faulted Xie and wished to apply the law to him.

value.zh: 論者多為有言，浚猶不釋。
value.en: Many pleaded for Shu Xie; Pan Jun still refused to relent.
value.literal: Though many debaters spoke on his behalf, Jun still would not release him.

value.zh: 鄰謂浚曰："舒伯膺兄弟爭死，海內義之，以為美談，仲膺又奉國舊意。
value.en: Sun Lin told Pan Jun: The Shu brothers once vied to die for honor—the empire admired it—and Zhongying still carries that loyalty.
value.literal: Lin said to Jun, The Shu brothers Boying contended to die for each other—the realm praised their righteousness as a fine tale—and Zhongying moreover embodies the state’s former intentions.

value.zh: 今君殺其子弟，若天下一統，青蓋北巡，中州士人必問仲膺繼嗣，答者雲潘承明殺燮，於事何如?"浚意即解，燮用得濟。
value.en: If you execute his kin and the empire is someday reunited, the north will ask after Zhongying’s heir—and answering Pan Jun killed Shu Xie will shame you. Pan Jun relented and Shu Xie was spared.
value.literal: Now if you kill his sons and nephews, should the realm unite and the imperial canopy tour north, gentlemen of the Central Plains will surely ask who succeeds Zhongying—if the answer is Pan Chengming killed Xie, how will that stand? Jun’s intent immediately loosened, and Xie obtained deliverance.

value.zh: 〈《博物志》曰：仲膺名邵。
value.en: 〈Bowuzhi: Zhongying’s personal name was Shao.
value.literal: 〈The Bowuzhi states: Zhongying’s given name was Shao.

value.zh: 初，伯膺亲友为人所杀，仲膺为报怨。
value.en: Boying’s kin had been murdered; Zhongying took revenge.
value.literal: At first Boying’s relatives were murdered by someone; Zhongying avenged the grievance.

value.zh: 事觉，兄弟争死，皆得免。
value.en: When discovered they argued over who should die; both were pardoned.
value.literal: When the affair was discovered the brothers vied to die; both were spared.

value.zh: 袁术时，邵为阜陵长。
value.en: Under Yuan Shu, Shao was magistrate of Fuling.
value.literal: During Yuan Shu’s time Shao was magistrate of Fuling.

value.zh: 亦见江表传。〉
value.en: The Jiangbiao zhuan records the same.〉
value.literal: It is also seen in the Jiangbiao zhuan.〉

value.zh: 鄰遷夏口沔中督、威遠將軍，所居任職。
value.en: Sun Lin rose to middle-Han–Xiakou inspector and General Who Deters the Distance, performing solid service.
value.literal: Lin was promoted inspector of Xiakou and the central Mian and General Who Deters the Distance, carrying out his duties where stationed.

value.zh: 赤烏十二年卒。
value.en: He died in Chiwu 12.
value.literal: He died in the twelfth year of Chiwu.

value.zh: 子苗嗣。
value.en: His son Sun Miao inherited.
value.literal: His son Miao succeeded.

value.zh: 苗弟旅及叔父安、熙、績，皆歷列位。
value.en: Sun Miao’s brother Sun Lü and uncles Sun An, Sun Xi, and Sun Ji all served in turn.
value.literal: Miao’s younger brother Lü and uncles An, Xi, and Ji all held successive offices.

value.zh: 〈吴历曰：邻又有子曰述，为武昌督，平荆州事。
value.en: 〈The Wu li notes another son, Shu, who commanded Wuchang and Jingzhou affairs.
value.literal: 〈The Wu li states: Lin also had a son named Shu, who was inspector of Wuchang and handled Jing Province affairs.

value.zh: 震，无难督。
value.en: Sun Zhen held the colonelcy Who Has No Difficulty.
value.literal: Zhen, Colonel Who Has No Difficulty.

value.zh: 谐，城门校尉。
value.en: Sun Xie was colonel of the Capital Gates.
value.literal: Xie, colonel of the Capital Gates.

value.zh: 歆，乐乡督。
value.en: Sun Xin commanded Lexiang.
value.literal: Xin, inspector of Lexiang.

value.zh: 震后御晋军，与张悌俱死。
value.en: Sun Zhen later faced the Jin host and fell beside Zhang Ti.
value.literal: Later Zhen opposed the Jin army and died together with Zhang Ti.

value.zh: 贲曾孙惠，字德施。
value.en: Sun Ben’s great-grandson Sun Hui, styled Deshi.
value.literal: Ben’s great-grandson Hui, courtesy name Deshi.

value.zh: 《惠别传》曰：惠好学有才智，晋永宁元年，赴齐王冏义，以功封晋兴侯，辟大司马贼曹属。
value.en: His appendix: Sun Hui was bookish and clever; in Jin Yongning 1 he joined Prince Sima Jiong’s righteous army, earned the marquisate of Jinxing, and entered the grand marshal’s criminal bureau.
value.literal: The Separate Biography of Hui states: Hui loved learning and had talent and judgment; in the first year of Yongning of Jin he answered Prince Qi of Qi’s call to righteousness and for merit was enfeoffed Marquis of Jinxing and summoned aide in the bandit bureau of the Grand Marshal.

value.zh: 冏骄矜僭侈，天下失望。
value.en: Sima Jiong grew arrogant and wasteful and forfeited the empire’s trust.
value.literal: Jiong was arrogant, presumptuous, and extravagant; the realm lost hope in him.

value.zh: 惠献言於冏，讽以五难、四不可，劝令委让万机，归籓青岱，辞甚深切。
value.en: Sun Hui remonstrated with the five difficulties and four impossibilities, urging him to surrender power and retire to his Shandong fief—in biting terms.
value.literal: Hui submitted advice to Jiong, using allegories of five difficulties and four impossibilities, urging him to yield the myriad affairs of state and return to his fief on Qing and Dai—the words were trenchant indeed.

value.zh: 冏不能纳，顷之果败。
value.en: Sima Jiong would not listen and soon fell.
value.literal: Jiong could not accept it; shortly afterward he indeed fell.

value.zh: 成都王颖召为大将军参军。
value.en: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying named him grand general’s aide.
value.literal: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying summoned him as aide to the Grand General.

value.zh: 是时颖将有事於长沙，以陆机为前锋都督。
value.en: Sima Ying was preparing a Changsha campaign and made Lu Ji vanguard commander.
value.literal: At that time Ying was about to undertake affairs at Changsha and made Lu Ji advance commander.

value.zh: 惠与机乡里亲厚，忧其致祸，谓之曰：“子盍让都督於王粹乎？”
value.en: Sun Hui, Lu Ji’s townsman and friend, feared ruin for him and asked: Why not give the command to Wang Cui.
value.literal: Hui was from the same village as Ji and close to him; fearing disaster for Ji, he said to him, Why not yield the commander’s post to Wang Cui?

value.zh: 机曰：“将谓吾避贼首鼠，更速其害。”
value.en: Lu Ji answered: They would call me a coward—that would only hasten disaster.
value.literal: Ji said, People would say I shrink from the enemy like a rat—that would hasten my ruin.

value.zh: 机寻被戮，二弟云、耽亦见杀，惠甚伤恨之。
value.en: Lu Ji was soon executed with his brothers Yun and Dan; Sun Hui mourned bitterly.
value.literal: Ji was shortly afterward executed; his two younger brothers Yun and Dan were also killed—Hui deeply grieved for them.

value.zh: 永兴元年，乘舆幸鄴，司空东海王越治兵下邳，惠以书干越，诡其姓名，自称南岳逸民秦祕之，勉以勤王匡世之略，辞义甚美。
value.en: In Yongxing 1 the court moved toward Ye; Prince Donghai Sima Yue trained troops at Xiapi. Sun Hui wrote under the pseudonym Southern Mountain hermit Qin Mizhi, urging him to rescue the throne.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongxing the imperial carriage favored Ye; Minister of Works Prince Donghai Sima Yue drilled troops at Xiapi—Hui wrote to Yue under a false name, calling himself the South Mountain recluse Qin Mizhi, urging with handsome phrases the strategy of aiding the king and restoring the age.

value.zh: 越省其书，榜题道衢，招求其人。
value.en: Sima Yue posted the essay at crossroads and hunted for the author.
value.literal: Yue read his letter, posted the title on the roads, and sought the man.

value.zh: 惠乃出见，越即以为记室参军，专掌文疏，豫参谋议。
value.en: Sun Hui revealed himself; Sima Yue made him secretary-aide for drafts and planning.
value.literal: Hui then came forward to meet him; Yue immediately made him secretary-aide, solely in charge of documents and participating in counsel.

value.zh: 每造书檄，越或驿马催之，应命立成，皆有辞旨。
value.en: When Sima Yue needed edicts he sometimes sent post riders—Sun Hui composed them on demand, always elegant.
value.literal: Whenever he drafted letters or proclamations, Yue sometimes sent relay horses to hurry him; he answered the summons on the spot and finished at once, each piece having polished rhetoric.

value.zh: 累迁显职，后为广武将军、安丰内史。
value.en: He climbed to high office and ended as campaigning General Who Displays Might and interior minister of Anfeng.
value.literal: He rose through prominent posts and later became General Who Displays Might on Campaign and interior minister of Anfeng.

value.zh: 年四十七卒。
value.en: He died at forty-seven.
value.literal: He died at forty-seven.

value.zh: 惠文翰凡數十首。
value.en: His writings ran to several dozen pieces.〉
value.literal: Hui’s literary compositions number several tens of pieces in all.〉

value.zh: 晉惠帝太安二年，成都王穎使陸機率眾向京師，擊長沙王乂。
value.en: In the second year of Tai'an, Emperor Hui of Jin's reign, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, ordered Lu Ji to march on the capital and strike the Prince of Changsha, Sima Ai.
value.literal: In the second year of Tai'an of Emperor Hui of Jin, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, sent Lu Ji at the head of an army toward the capital to attack the Prince of Changsha, Sima Ai.

value.zh: 軍始引而牙竿折，俄而戰敗，機被誅。
value.en: The army had barely moved when the command pennant pole broke; shortly afterward the force was routed and Lu Ji was put to death.
value.literal: As soon as the army set out the command pennant staff snapped; soon afterward they were defeated and Ji was executed.

value.zh: 穎尋奔潰，卒賜死。
value.en: Ying soon fled in defeat and was eventually compelled to commit suicide.
value.literal: Ying soon fled in rout and in the end was ordered to take his own life.

value.zh: 初，河間王顒謀先誅長沙，廢太子，立穎。
value.en: Earlier the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, had planned to kill the Prince of Changsha first, depose the crown prince, and set up Ying in his place.
value.literal: Earlier the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, had plotted first to kill the Prince of Changsha, depose the heir, and install Ying.

value.zh: 長沙知之，誅其黨卞粹等，故穎來伐。
value.en: The Prince of Changsha uncovered the plot and executed Yong's allies Bian Cui and the rest, which brought Ying's invasion.
value.literal: The Prince of Changsha learned of it and executed his partisans Bian Cui and others; therefore Ying came to attack.

value.zh: 機又以穎得遐邇心，將為漢之代王，遂委質於穎，為犯從之將。
value.en: Lu Ji likewise believed Ying had won universal support and would replace the Han house as king; he therefore pledged himself to Ying and served as a general in the rebel host.
value.literal: Ji also thought that because Ying had won the hearts of near and far he would become the Han dynasty's replacement king, and therefore submitted to Ying and served as a general who followed the rebel cause.

value.zh: 此皆姦謀之罰，木不曲直也。
value.en: All of this fell under the penalty for treacherous designs—wood failing to be straight or bent.
value.literal: All these were punishments for treacherous plots—wood not straight or bent.

value.zh: 晉惠帝元康中，賈謐親貴，數入二宮，與儲君遊戲，无降下心。
value.en: During Yuankang, Jia Mi, riding on intimate favor, entered the inner palaces again and again to sport with the crown prince and showed no deference.
value.literal: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of Jin, Jia Mi enjoyed intimate favor and repeatedly entered the two palaces to play with the heir apparent, without a submissive heart.

value.zh: 又嘗同弈棊爭道，成都王穎厲色曰：「皇太子，國之儲貳。
value.en: Once, disputing a game of go, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, said sharply: "The crown prince is the heir of the realm.
value.literal: Once when they played go and disputed the board, the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, said sternly: "The crown prince is the state's heir.

value.zh: 賈謐何敢無禮！」
value.en: How dare Jia Mi behave without courtesy!"
value.literal: How dare Jia Mi be discourteous!"

value.zh: 謐猶不悛，故及於禍。
value.en: Mi still would not mend his ways, and so brought disaster on himself.
value.literal: Mi still did not reform himself; therefore he met with disaster.

value.zh: 昔黃帝有子二十五人，或內列諸華，或外分荒服，昌意少子，受封北土，國有大鮮卑山，因以為號。
value.en: Long ago the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons: some served within the Chinese heartland, others were sent to govern the outer marches. Changyi, his youngest, was enfeoffed in the north, where the great Xianbei Mountain stood—and from that mountain the people took their name.
value.literal: In olden times the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons; some were enrolled within the Chinese domains, some were apportioned to distant borderlands. Changyi was his youngest son; he received a fief in the northern lands. The state had the great Xianbei Mountain, and from it took its name.

value.zh: 其後，世為君長，統幽都之北，廣漠之野，畜牧遷徙，射獵為業，淳樸為俗，簡易為化，不為文字，刻木紀契而已，世事遠近，人相傳授，如史官之紀錄焉。
value.en: Afterward they ruled generation upon generation north of Youdu, across the wide steppe. They lived by herding, moving with the seasons, and by the hunt; their ways were plain, their customs unadorned. They had no script—only notches cut in wood to seal bargains. What happened near and far was handed down mouth to mouth, much as if scribes had kept annals.
value.literal: Thereafter generation after generation they were chieftains, ruling north of Youdu in the vast deserts. Pastoral migration and hunting were their livelihood; simplicity their custom, plainness their transformation. They did not use writing, but only carved wood to record agreements. Affairs near and far were passed from person to person, like the records of historians.

value.zh: 黃帝以土德王，北俗謂土為托，謂后為跋，故以為氏。
value.en: The Yellow Emperor reigned under the virtue of Earth; northerners called earth tuo and called a queen ba—so the clan took the name Tuoba.
value.literal: The Yellow Emperor ruled by the virtue of Earth; in northern custom earth was called tuo and a queen was called ba, hence they took it as their clan name.

value.zh: 其裔始均，入仕堯世，逐女魃於弱水之北，民賴其勤，帝舜嘉之，命為田祖。
value.en: A descendant, Shijun, served in the reign of Yao, driving the drought demon Nüba beyond the Weak Water. The people owed their relief to his labor; Shun commended him and named him Lord of the Fields.
value.literal: His descendant Shijun entered service in the age of Yao, drove Nüba north of the Weak Water; the people relied on his diligence, Emperor Shun praised him, and appointed him Lord of the Fields.

value.zh: 爰歷三代，以及秦漢，獯鬻、獫狁、山戎、匈奴之屬，累代殘暴，作害中州，而始均之裔，不交南夏，是以載籍無聞焉。
value.en: Through the Three Dynasties and on into Qin and Han, the Xiongnu and their kindred peoples—Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong—ravaged the Central Plains generation after generation. Yet Shijun's line never dealt with the southern realms, and so the written histories say nothing of them.
value.literal: Thus through the Three Dynasties down to Qin and Han, the Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong, Xiongnu and their kind were generation after generation violent, harming the Central States—but the descendants of Shijun did not mingle with Southern Xia, and therefore they go unmentioned in written records.

value.zh: 二年，葬文帝及皇后封氏。
value.en: In the second year they interred Emperor Wen and Empress Feng.
value.literal: In the second year they buried Emperor Wen and Empress Lady Feng.

value.zh: 初，思帝欲改葬，未果而崩。
value.en: Earlier Emperor Si had planned a reburial, but died before it could be done.
value.literal: Earlier Emperor Si had wished to rebury them, but before accomplishing it he died.

value.zh: 至是，述成前意焉。
value.en: At last they carried out what he had intended.
value.literal: Now they fulfilled his earlier intention.

value.zh: 晉成都王司馬穎遣從事中郎田思，河間王司馬顒遣司馬靳利，并州刺史司馬騰遣主簿梁天，並來會葬。
value.en: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, sent Tian Si as attendant-in-ordinary; Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, sent Commandant Jin Li; Sima Teng, inspector of Bingzhou, sent registrar Liang Tian—all to attend the burial.
value.literal: Sima Ying the Prince of Chengdu sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Tian Si; Sima Yong the Prince of Hejian sent Commandant Jin Li; Sima Teng the Inspector of Bingzhou sent Registrar Liang Tian—all came for the funeral.

value.zh: 遠近赴者二十萬人。
value.en: Nearly two hundred thousand mourners came from near and far.
value.literal: From near and far two hundred thousand came to attend.

value.zh: 十年，晉惠帝為成都王穎逼留在鄴。
value.en: In the tenth year Emperor Hui of Jin was held at Ye by Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu.
value.literal: In the tenth year Emperor Hui of Jin was compelled by Sima Ying the Prince of Chengdu to remain at Ye.

value.zh: 匈奴別種劉淵反於離石，自號漢王。
value.en: Liu Yuan, of a Xiongnu splinter line, rose at Lishi and proclaimed himself King of Han.
value.literal: Liu Yuan, a separate branch of the Xiongnu, rebelled at Lishi and styled himself King of Han.

value.zh: 并州刺史司馬騰來乞師，桓帝率十餘萬騎，帝亦同時大舉以助之，大破淵眾於西河、上黨。
value.en: Sima Teng, inspector of Bingzhou, begged for aid. Emperor Huan led more than a hundred thousand cavalry, and Emperor Zhao mobilized on the same scale; together they shattered Liu Yuan's forces at Xihe and Shangdang.
value.literal: Sima Teng, Inspector of Bingzhou, came to beg troops; Emperor Huan led more than a hundred thousand horse, and the emperor also launched a great campaign at the same time to assist, thoroughly defeating Liu Yuan's host at Xihe and Shangdang.

value.zh: 會惠帝還洛，騰乃辭師。
value.en: When Emperor Hui was restored to Luoyang, Teng released the allied troops.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui returned to Luoyang, Teng then dismissed the army.

value.zh: 桓帝與騰盟於汾東而還。
value.en: Emperor Huan swore alliance with Teng east of the Fen River and marched home.
value.literal: Emperor Huan made alliance with Teng east of the Fen and returned.

value.zh: 乃使輔相衞雄、段繁，於參合陂西累石為亭，樹碑以記行焉。
value.en: He had his ministers Wei Xiong and Duan Fan raise a stone pavilion west of Canhe Marsh and erect a stele to commemorate the campaign.
value.literal: He sent his aides Wei Xiong and Duan Fan west of Canhepo to pile stones into a pavilion and set up a stele to record the journey.

value.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷
value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83

value.zh: 散騎常侍賈謐侍講東宮，對太子倨傲，成都王穎見而叱之；
value.en: Jia Mi, Regular Attendant Within the Encampment, lectured in the Eastern Palace and treated the heir apparent with insolence. Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, witnessed it and rebuked him;
value.literal: Jia Mi, Regular Attendant Within the Encampment, lectured in the Eastern Palace and was arrogant toward the Heir Apparent; the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, saw it and rebuked him;

value.zh: 謐怒，言於賈后，出穎為平北將軍，鎮鄴。
value.en: Furious, Mi complained to Empress Jia, who had Ying transferred out as General Who Pacifies the North and posted to Ye.
value.literal: Mi grew angry and spoke to Empress Jia, who sent Ying out as General Who Pacifies the North, stationed at Ye.

value.zh: 征梁王肜為大將軍、錄尚書事；
value.en: Sima Rong, Prince of Liang, was summoned to serve as Grand General and Recorder of the Masters of Writing;
value.literal: The Prince of Liang, Sima Rong, was summoned as Grand General and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing;

value.zh: 以河間王顒為鎮西將軍，鎮關中。
value.en: and Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, was appointed General Who Guards the West to hold Guanzhong.
value.literal: the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, was made General Who Guards the West and stationed in Guanzhong.

value.zh: 初，武帝作石函之制，非至親不得鎮關中；
value.en: Earlier Emperor Wu had decreed in the stone casket that only the closest imperial kin might garrison Guanzhong;
value.literal: Earlier Emperor Wu had established the stone-casket rule: none but the closest kin might garrison Guanzhong;

value.zh: 顒輕財愛士，朝廷以為賢，故用之。
value.en: but Yong was generous and cultivated men of talent, so the court considered him worthy and appointed him anyway.
value.literal: Yong was generous with wealth and cherished scholars; the court regarded him as worthy and therefore employed him.
